name: Houston Gaines
subject: The Latest Updates from the Gold Dome
body:
Read up-to-date information from the Capitol
| | | | |
---
| As we head into the final days of the 2026 legislative Session, we're focused on cutting taxes, strengthening public safety, and advancing key priorities for Georgia families. While we've already passed a number of bills, there is still a lot to be done in the next few days. This week will be bittersweet as it will mark my eighth and final legislative Session when we adjourn Sine Die. Please read below for the latest updates from under the Gold Dome.
---
| |
---
| LEGISLATIVE UPDATES
---
|
---
| Over the past two weeks, the Georgia General Assembly has taken significant action on legislation aimed at providing financial relief and addressing key priorities across our state. One of the most notable measures we passed was House Bill 1199, which includes a 60-day suspension of Georgia's excise tax on motor fuel. This comes at a critical time as fuel prices rise, placing added pressure on families and businesses. The suspension will save consumers 33.3 cents per gallon on gasoline and 37.3 cents on diesel, and with Governor Kemp already signing it into law, Georgians can expect relief at the pump as new fuel shipments arrive.
Another major priority was House Bill 1000, which delivers additional tax relief through a one-time $1 billion income tax refund. Also now signed into law, this measure applies to taxpayers who filed returns for the 2024 and 2025 tax years. Eligible individuals will receive $250 for single filers or $375 for married individuals filing separately or $500 for married couples filing jointly. This marks the fourth consecutive year the General Assembly has approved one-time tax refunds, reinforcing our commitment to ensuring economic growth directly benefits Georgia families.
In recent years, the General Assembly and Governor have returned over $11 billion directly back to Georgia's taxpayers while continuing to pass a balanced budget each year.
We also recently advanced policies focused on education and student success. House Bill 1009 would prohibit cell phone use for high school students in public schools during the school day beginning in 2027, with limited exceptions for medical or educational needs. By requiring schools to enforce these policies, our goal is to reduce distractions and improve academic focus in the classroom.
In addition, we passed a number of public safety measures. Senate Bill 443 increases penalties for obstructing highways and public passages and allows affected individuals to pursue civil damages. Senate Bill 605 enhances oversight of prosecutors by establishing clearer standards for discipline or removal, continuing our efforts to crack down on rogue district attorneys. Senate Bill 547 continues our efforts to combat human trafficking by making pimping and pandering felony offenses in all cases. Senate Bill 442 would provide for the automatic revocation of a noncitizen's commercial driver's license upon the expiration of their visa and require noncitizens to pass the applicable knowledge and skills tests to renew their commercial driver's licenses. This bill aims to address issues we've seen across the nation of trucking accidents involving foreign drivers unable to read traffic signage.
---
| |
---
| In addition to these headline measures, the House also passed a number of other bills, including:
* SB 433: Allows individuals with autism or developmental disabilities to obtain a voluntary specialty license plate and provides law enforcement with training to improve safety and communication during encounters.
* SB 403: Streamlines the process for Georgians to recover unclaimed property, making government more efficient and responsive.
* SB 542: Creates new criminal penalties for clergy who engage in sexual conduct with individuals under their spiritual authority, strengthening protections for victims.
* SB 540 & SB 594: Establish safeguards against AI misuse by protecting minors, requiring transparency and creating penalties for deceptive uses like election interference and exploitation.
* HB 1030: The Math Matters Act expands access to advanced math, increases instructional time and improves teacher training while giving parents flexibility in placement decisions.
* SB 452: Enhances retirement benefits for law enforcement by increasing employer contributions to 401(k) plans based on years of service.

Each year, our sole Constitutional duty is to the pass a balanced budget. The House and Senate have now each passed our own versions of the Fiscal Year 2027 (July 1, 2026-June 30, 2027) budget. Now the two chambers are working on hashing out differences so that we can give final approval before we complete this year's Session on Thursday. I look forward to sharing with you the details of the budget as it is finalized in the coming days.
---
| |
---
| EVENTS AND VISITORS
---
| |
---
| |
---
| |
---
| Over the past few weeks, I've enjoyed traveling throughout the district and connecting with so many individuals and groups when not at the Capitol. Last weekend, Gabi and I attended the UGA Great Southland Stampede Rodeo and the Oconee County Republican Party's Stumping Ground. I also had the pleasure of speaking to the Barrow County monthly GOP gathering, as well as attending a meaningful veterans event in Putnam County.
If there is ever an event in our community where you'd like for me to attend or speak, please reach out and let us know. If you are near the Capitol this week, I invite you to join us in the final days of the Session to see your legislature at work.
---
| |
---
| |
---
| |
---
| On Thursday, I joined House colleagues in celebrating the retirement of the Speaker Pro Tempore of the House, Jan Jones. Jan has been my seat mate in the House for the last eight years and has been a mentor to me. She's made me and many others in the General Assembly more effective legislators. More importantly, she's a great person and friend. Her years of dedicated service have left a lasting impact on our state and the people of Georgia. Please join me in thanking Jan for her service!
---
| |
---
| |
---
| PAGE PROGRAM
---
| I enjoyed welcoming two pages at the Capitol last week - Georgie Howell and Zola Graves. The page program gives students the opportunity to spend a day with us in the House, learning firsthand about the work we do under the Gold Dome and how state government operates. We're grateful to these outstanding students for taking the time to visit the Capitol and for their interest in being involved and engaged in the legislative process.
---
| |
---
| |
---
| |
---
| WHAT'S NEXT?
---
| We are entering the final stretch of our 40-day legislative Session. With Sine Die this Thursday, we are focused on working with the Senate to finalize outstanding legislation, including our state's annual budget.
As always, I stand ready to assist with any questions, comments, or concerns you may have--please don't hesitate to reach out. Thank you for the honor of serving as your State Representative!
---

body:
I never intended for things to end up like this. All I wanted to do was keep serving my country, the same way I have since I was sworn in to the U.S. Navy.

[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/128371604/611115545/-2000534896?amount=10&refcode=LOC_EM_FR_2026.03.30_Mark-Kelly-Split_B1_F1_S1_C1_90OP_N-T0&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODg1OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2MTdjMGJhZS00YjJjLWYxMTEtOWE0OC0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=VLJaAxsHhA4r15NlEgiAKOlpdvwknbFVdoLBjXSb8U4=) Team, when Gabby and I first agreed that I would run for Senate back in 2019, we knew things would change. We know more than most how public service can change your life.

But I’ve got to tell you, I never intended for things to end up like this. All I wanted to do was keep serving my country, the same way I have since I was sworn in to the U.S. Navy.

I know that service comes with risk, sure. But I didn’t set out to be threatened with a court-martial by the Secretary of Defense, or to have the President of the United States calling for my execution.

Look, I don’t want you to worry about me. I’ve been through a lot in my life, and things like this don’t intimidate me all that much.

I do worry that Trump might succeed at intimidating others, though. Like people just beginning to get involved, or thinking about joining a peaceful demonstration, or speaking out at a town hall. I worry Trump and his cronies are trying to scare people out of resisting him.

But then I see millions of people meeting this moment with the courage and resolve it demands of them. People like my friend Maggie Hassan. It makes me hopeful, sure. But more than that, it makes me incredibly proud.

We’re ready to fight like hell to save our democracy. If you’re with me, please:

But I didn’t set out to be threatened with a court-martial by the Secretary of Defense, or to have the President of the United States calling for my execution. Look, I don’t want you to worry about me. I’ve been through a lot in my life, and things like this don’t intimidate me all that much. Lately, I've been doing some reflecting on my grandfather, President John F. Kennedy, and his legacy of hope.
In my run to fight for NY-12 in Congress, and just as a person, that's what I want to focus on. Hope.
My name is Jack, or John Bouvier Kennedy Schlossberg if you want to know the whole thing.
In high school, I spent hours watching my grandfather's speeches. He taught us all that politics isn't about serving yourself — it's about serving others. When we fight for hope, we're not just doing it for ourselves, we're doing it for each other and the future we all have to share.
I know I have big shoes to fill. In my grandfather's memory, I've led a life of caring about this a lot. I put that care and effort and hope into everything I do.
But this is bigger than me. It's bigger than my family's legacy.
Hope is hard to find in Politics these days, but if we let it die out completely, that's how we really lose. Now cannot be the time to stop caring or turn away. We have to double down in our pursuit of hope.
I really think this election is the one — our last chance to stop Trump and change the direction we're heading in.
I need you to know that I believe we can do it. I believe in hope, and I believe in us. Will you believe with me? In a recent conversation between a colleague of mine and a candidate running for state legislature, the candidate was asked about his views on several policy issues. He was thoughtful, open, and willing to explain his beliefs. But then he added a caveat that should concern every voter: once elected, he said, he would be obligated to vote however the majority of his district wanted--regardless of whether it conflicted with his own judgment or principles.
This may sound democratic, even virtuous. In reality, it reflects a fundamental misunderstanding of what it means to serve in a representative republic.
In our system, citizens do not elect legislators to function as human polling machines. They elect representatives to exercise judgment on their behalf within the constraints of a constitution. Those representatives are accountable to voters at election time, but while in office they are sworn to uphold the constitution, respect limits on government power, and protect individual rights--even when doing so is unpopular.
The idea that an elected official must always follow the immediate will of the majority is closer to direct democracy than representative government. History shows why that distinction matters. Majorities are not infallible. They can be misinformed, driven by fear, or motivated by short-term passions. Without restraint, majority rule easily becomes majority tyranny.
If a legislator believes he must vote for any policy his district demands, then constitutional protections become optional. Free speech, due process, property rights, and equal protection all become subject to popular vote. That is precisely what constitutions exist to prevent. Rights are not supposed to hinge on whether they are fashionable or politically convenient.
This mindset also creates a convenient escape hatch for politicians. "My hands were tied," they say. "My district made me do it." In practice, this often becomes a way to justify voting against principles they claim to hold, while avoiding responsibility for the consequences. Leadership is replaced with blame-shifting, and conviction gives way to convenience.
True representation requires more courage than that. It means listening to constituents, understanding their concerns, and taking them seriously--but not surrendering independent judgment. It means explaining difficult votes, defending unpopular positions, and trusting voters to decide whether that judgment deserves another term. Accountability comes at the ballot box, not through daily referendums.
The Founders understood this well. They designed a system meant to slow down rash decisions, elevate deliberation, and protect liberty from both authoritarian rulers and unchecked majorities. A legislator who does not understand this role--or worse, openly rejects it--poses a real risk to constitutional government.
Voters should be wary of candidates who promise to "just vote how the district wants." That promise may feel empowering, but it ultimately weakens the very safeguards that protect minority rights, economic stability, and the rule of law. We should expect more from those who seek office--not blind obedience to opinion polls, but informed judgment grounded in principle and constitutional restraint.
A representative republic depends not just on good laws, but on legislators who understand why those laws exist--and who are willing to uphold them, even when it's hard.

Allow me to introduce myself to you |
---

Peter,

You may already know who I am from my basketball career. Or, maybe you’re just hearing about me for the first time through my Senate Campaign. Either way, I wanted to formally introduce myself and share my story. [**_Afterward, I’m going to ask you to send a small contribution to my campaign as I continue to fight to Flip Minnesota Red._**](https://links.iterable.com/u/click?_t=ce1ce9e616484205a28a45cfaf96cecf&_m=9a6d7defcbb747ddb2a86bb2a6799543&_e=pL6hGc3chrwx2Qsj8TTZVEkhhJmVmMWOjFps2cBHJ9e7Pd6jgLVuQhsfeqRm5dRNMu1gA726EQO-XNjI-6VTCNTPVIN5oRoDuLk8SjgJaLEu5UMgVrW3C-XOAFV6rvLihmgzjv3B87301IIjTYnRNrho8n0n4CD9aQUt-pTtRnkqzd2aheJI7Iqr99Ay-GMHHFYnOTPP75xv9Bk-dGZ3BuJG03QSgeYDNMjr5A1vWyUiKgpLEJwDInRAe9hDkZftVDnvJVG4TfI243X1u0ybqyV3TQqsH8pVTkKC5Pvqr9pL563E1Y2SRU5DArPOMIyofs_W0702QHjgotzeBBFjC44FnEYZNDAXq6B5tFF_2Awd5QK5EEBsKnTrxwpzJ8xybf6s_dexKQdtrhIl6-4-0QKZ3FaqlfhKggI5rjZEzPXom0igjpqXOyL7L5vftQLXTvHcGoz33ltC1KvFG3hnsK4UV_71zAOp3cTEGzcTZbUB-ux8KL1TihSICkMmuIvU1VkaTatiYTy4GnKun3k5N_KOL2g0b9clMYUwoE88yL6ENGuieQJ93-HpWllwUC-g)

I was born and raised in the Twin Cities in Minnesota, mainly in the Rondo Community of St. Paul. At the age of five, I started playing sports, and at nine years old, I was already playing basketball on the Northside of Minneapolis. My mother was a single mother who worked tirelessly to give me a better life. I went to school in Rondo and began to excel at basketball. By 10th grade, I was ranked as a top 20 player in the country. I remember dreaming of reaching the NBA one day– a dream shared by millions of kids.

[](https://links.iterable.com/u/click?_t=ce1ce9e616484205a28a45cfaf96cecf&_m=9a6d7defcbb747ddb2a86bb2a6799543&_e=pL6hGc3chrwx2Qsj8TTZVEkhhJmVmMWOjFps2cBHJ9e7Pd6jgLVuQhsfeqRm5dRNMu1gA726EQO-XNjI-6VTCNTPVIN5oRoDuLk8SjgJaLEu5UMgVrW3C-XOAFV6rvLihmgzjv3B87301IIjTYnRNrho8n0n4CD9aQUt-pTtRnkqzd2aheJI7Iqr99Ay-GMHiiUT7OT3NXPumcWDmlRpkF-KDKBk_5v9sxZuzIoM18GaUDStTw-1qbuzG5_8W3G6ySdjycLNh2hvCkpyKAuVfCEIj8jOG-0zLFwPoVvk2LevIPOWUnk_8o4-31CjwDSsqNnEvP9BNKyi2QeSsUb3BJ2Z1-TMwI427UfmF7zrCR8TobHKuXejQAMvFTwrdXu7klSXmd0danrLTxr9d60_5QrVzem7EEsuRIt4DbWQ6VzZp1ta0DesqQyBplAg2NN9O-ZyVTSNnREz7NLwVWPEJQgKZHsyBcMV7FUVkDwaec-jMfAjcS2MytPyDoq_6mGvUlOl9CT7FwG6l-wib8I7FC8F3DW1kPJj7QgnAQmCsW0x9mVodTGRWhsn2s1xT7TO)
I accepted a scholarship at the University of Minnesota, but shortly after transferred to Iowa State. There, I won multiple basketball awards while working hard in class and being named on the Dean’s List for academics.

[](https://links.iterable.com/u/click?_t=ce1ce9e616484205a28a45cfaf96cecf&_m=9a6d7defcbb747ddb2a86bb2a6799543&_e=pL6hGc3chrwx2Qsj8TTZVEkhhJmVmMWOjFps2cBHJ9e7Pd6jgLVuQhsfeqRm5dRNMu1gA726EQO-XNjI-6VTCNTPVIN5oRoDuLk8SjgJaLEu5UMgVrW3C-XOAFV6rvLihmgzjv3B87301IIjTYnRNrho8n0n4CD9aQUt-pTtRnkqzd2aheJI7Iqr99Ay-GMHbMHX69lgfSIAsok9PsBEu8xNDUL6qlN3R-n1KN5-St1WgRBWLHQRxlriegEi3g7-mdJWVnEl6WVAuwj4zFCxmSWrXuDp_1LiClOamAXNaHtnv8WYPVpDx0DpGzEUIInbbOaIJmqW8bOL0u8OS0mJMLJIm4NvYQLI3-8O3k_ONP2B9to3xKHBID63jqDxeqOIKL0rWpkP0BMz5_Qby4PC0FRLvtofhLrLc-Op1yAew1wXPElxqsK8L85nTfMzfs8jWcs5Jq04Ix5_uV7EJZnQcQOkIvNjjmLElKFJMLKaWPcgzrlnIbK7j1eYvWqVMZZKu-rH4p0QjRcAv2VeYIFQCTkqP_2sjrXbzo0Uy_B-P2qEB1KGgkH_UXqRDj2_PqPR)
Finally, my dream came true. I was selected in the first round of the 2012 NBA Draft, going to the Houston Rockets. While playing at the highest level of basketball competition in the world, I began to voice concerns about the NBA’s Collective Bargaining Agreement (CBA), specifically regarding mental health policy, which at the time did not exist.

Eventually, my concerns became a dispute between the NBA and myself, until I demanded that the NBA spearhead the mental health conversation through policy. This led to the end of my NBA career, but my work led to the NBA implementing policies to support players’ mental health.

[](https://links.iterable.com/u/click?_t=ce1ce9e616484205a28a45cfaf96cecf&_m=9a6d7defcbb747ddb2a86bb2a6799543&_e=pL6hGc3chrwx2Qsj8TTZVEkhhJmVmMWOjFps2cBHJ9e7Pd6jgLVuQhsfeqRm5dRNMu1gA726EQO-XNjI-6VTCNTPVIN5oRoDuLk8SjgJaLEu5UMgVrW3C-XOAFV6rvLihmgzjv3B87301IIjTYnRNrho8n0n4CD9aQUt-pTtRnkqzd2aheJI7Iqr99Ay-GMH1NDh5YKyvmUpIh8MHYCZ-39GnNHWkBqUiASMqgVBmSPtQ3lGosquWlymcUj__OLJbJzsZQiEbsd0GAca77rCX8Ca72WFpNnLgbzZ3HwkuRwxVmJMvmgHKiHIgxGis9xylhgxkG7oIr8g7s2W7W58fnyu7qqxcaUi4bndmC6pVXcOnvGpGKd-nrRRXNRnHQnaG1ByMVyMqDlXf8c5_opv3ef-K40Dh_xoHq42svLBdSp6tEOvC84RIxrdGr_ekZJJdcP5fxWAB7brpGYTtCzfRN_7exABa49G9TlrgKDXwCB2l0EOGt0xasFPxRMlgGdF9d9yOXoixKpfGDajNWUlQH17MXJORuubq-6yi3CsYZ_tEsqSUOUXW8G10AJAzRDu)
I gave up my dream of playing in the NBA to stand up for something I fully believe in. That experience gave me the courage to run for Congress in 2022 and for Senate in 2024. More on that later.

After leaving the NBA, I took my talents to Canada, playing professional basketball and winning two championships. Then, I joined the BIG 3 Basketball Tournament, a professional 3 on 3 league; I still play today.

[](https://links.iterable.com/u/click?_t=ce1ce9e616484205a28a45cfaf96cecf&_m=9a6d7defcbb747ddb2a86bb2a6799543&_e=pL6hGc3chrwx2Qsj8TTZVEkhhJmVmMWOjFps2cBHJ9e7Pd6jgLVuQhsfeqRm5dRNMu1gA726EQO-XNjI-6VTCNTPVIN5oRoDuLk8SjgJaLEu5UMgVrW3C-XOAFV6rvLihmgzjv3B87301IIjTYnRNrho8n0n4CD9aQUt-pTtRnkqzd2aheJI7Iqr99Ay-GMHOOHYiP1ii8jvtADlXhWwh4ykgH_XpvD8A0UVIcM741wsMS6yh4k-DQPe8koRTOU9H1m4LVT7gR-m9glgJ0JvH9Kv1dKElueyyACz4keNhbOH8gyrgmNKBKzhz853IbaHoe4U4PEBT27DQTUNpOmhDiXQGkpG02Q3kdlPNaZp4I5vNyhu3RDUcyVl1fSZCRn1MgUtmTcDFjeO6mFI1Wgq44UNG_8cdT2mSWZv4bneN-Xy7iQTMrv_4-27lEVT4THkH8uOZQaq6jP2Y4oY6wIN_lCPsiJqszlJSbpFzjJ26QjD26uAtOzK866FTsYT0xhwAXGticEbUwK1qP7n6g2M5JQPvtgQ6g5F509WzubVDeeR4f4xXNm3JEURWdNHt-Cs)
It was at this point that I became increasingly vocal about standing up for the core principles that I believe in. I’ve continued to be outspoken on taboo subjects, like freeing the Uyghurs, the Federal Reserve, Julian Assange, Edward Snowden, Muammar Gaddafi, and many others. **I’m not afraid to speak up and say the silent part out loud. I will never just shut up and dribble.**

In 2022, I decided to run for Congress against Radical Leftist and Squad Founder, Ilhan Omar. The Deep State Democrats lined her pocket with millions of dollars to beat me, and I came up short.

[](https://links.iterable.com/u/click?_t=ce1ce9e616484205a28a45cfaf96cecf&_m=9a6d7defcbb747ddb2a86bb2a6799543&_e=pL6hGc3chrwx2Qsj8TTZVEkhhJmVmMWOjFps2cBHJ9e7Pd6jgLVuQhsfeqRm5dRNMu1gA726EQO-XNjI-6VTCNTPVIN5oRoDuLk8SjgJaLEu5UMgVrW3C-XOAFV6rvLihmgzjv3B87301IIjTYnRNrho8n0n4CD9aQUt-pTtRnkqzd2aheJI7Iqr99Ay-GMHMo6ENOeX8ZwhSgqC39VESeWbf4KCPaLKr7_Wzm01jdS3ujPeb3loYji9PWZjq0wrBVGEHqk9ctYgvwoLqsSHaDBoKd0fo0tzwMnFInqOVUT2inRjefLZ8qA0DXeWOFzKuuhYBLGxrPCCfn-YJdfJhxBgyFKxwCUPQJigANJo7gSVenO0Ztv_Iz_sX9dE1A_9oMuv8c5gK3rNiZoqCngmvTZ8LAgNEioXUTXKG1XEP0vwWRRYRYcOQaFE5iW_oFpyQWZjXTkFBSLCgMRieVtG2JUUSjEP4nNZXbKCMvsoR-ayVTD5lZpmf-PGxtd09hCGkQ051XNfP8CaVxAXICmKffJo34UnLuInyF5d1huFY4CTbObmh9RkmbuFnxFKDWj_)
Now, I’m running for United States Senate to defeat RINO Michele Tafoya. She represents the Establishment who would rather see America become the next Communist China or Soviet Russia. The Industrial Media Complex will continue to spread false narratives claiming that I have little chance of winning. But they continue to ignore my strong grassroots movement with the American People, who are sick and tired of being overstepped, ignored, and told to accept the policies that our Liberal Leaders force down our throats.

We CAN win, but it’s going to take the help of a huge grassroots movement. That’s why I’m emailing you today, Peter. We have a chance to make history by electing the youngest US Senator and the first one born in the 1990s.

[**I am humbly asking you to send my campaign a small donation of whatever you can afford. Whether it’s $5, $15, or $25, every single donation makes a difference.**](https://links.iterable.com/u/click?_t=ce1ce9e616484205a28a45cfaf96cecf&_m=9a6d7defcbb747ddb2a86bb2a6799543&_e=pL6hGc3chrwx2Qsj8TTZVEkhhJmVmMWOjFps2cBHJ9e7Pd6jgLVuQhsfeqRm5dRNMu1gA726EQO-XNjI-6VTCNTPVIN5oRoDuLk8SjgJaLEu5UMgVrW3C-XOAFV6rvLihmgzjv3B87301IIjTYnRNrho8n0n4CD9aQUt-pTtRnkqzd2aheJI7Iqr99Ay-GMHSUjbhjES8Wjw7RoMdtKxusKrZb6UCc0aWe-xIkXAuaH213in6C-JKqLSP3mHgRMQF7JVKGrT5iplsN7mX4G32ONF_AuMn3cRUALpbHJtjf-p6-O8_mfiYTGIBw-Lm3M56PcWS7EIrq_Pbt9sd_uTUegaCLGl4-L1yargacdTd6idhs65rfEEmiWAPOIL_QX5gD8HocZxpkDwzU7Sj6Tx1vTiVLbqZv7vhpzau9pSlT-yE0g8TSL_7qnjVBtPtSpCke9VvlgrIWDogt_02xFwNsYs4Kc4yoRHPPDtG9O0IZYkF-3MaupjjEPSJ69eMtOxlSjSM_uk1abE0vtmn5c-6DVoSXaGwcCtLRYhv3u0NOz_22Lz68aIU-LlVeJ2T6hC)

I’m looking forward to getting to know you better, and I hope you’ll join my team.

Talk Soon,

Royce White

**" We will not stop until we have answers.**"
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/746ad90c-1b3d-473f-b467-25e4fca66cb3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
That's what Maine Secretary of State Shenna Bellows (D) said after _[The Robinson Report](https://substack.com/redirect/53363978-e010-4b73-a9ff-6974b82e9fcb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_[revealed](https://substack.com/redirect/53363978-e010-4b73-a9ff-6974b82e9fcb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that Maine's absentee ballot system had suffered the worst ever breach of election integrity.
Frau Bellows' Shermanesque declaration appears to have been a lie. Like when she told the Veterans and Legal Affairs Committee that she didn't admit to Marc Elias that non-citizens are registered to vote in Maine when in fact there's [video of her](https://substack.com/redirect/56230e59-f0d2-4f6d-b363-b342fe915ff1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) admitting exactly that.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/53363978-e010-4b73-a9ff-6974b82e9fcb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)| | |
#### [Maine Woman Finds Bundles of Election Ballots in Amazon Package](https://substack.com/redirect/53363978-e010-4b73-a9ff-6974b82e9fcb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
---
| | [The Robinson Report](https://substack.com/profile/147548156-the-robinson-report)| | *
---|---|---
| October 1, 2025
| [| Read full story
---](https://substack.com/redirect/53363978-e010-4b73-a9ff-6974b82e9fcb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
For those who have forgotten, 250 Maine absentee ballots arrived at a random home in Newburgh in an Amazon Prime package delivered via UPS. Bellows promised a swift resolution to the election crisis. She assured us the Maine State Police detectives assigned to work for her office would be getting to the bottom of the scandal. Then she said it would be the FBI. That might have been another fib, because no one in Newburgh was ever contacted by the FBI. At the last update, Bellows said the case was in the trustworthy and reliable hands of Maine Attorney General Aaron Frey.
[Insert the laugh-track...]
Only one person involved in the election breach has ever been interviewed -- the package recipient, the same person Bellows smeared at her debacle State House press conference. A motor vehicle detective interviewed the woman shortly after she turned the ballots over to her local election officials in the same way a local cop might take down some notes about area youths riding dirt bikes across her yard. But no one else in Newburgh has been interviewed, and the package recipient never talked to anyone at the FBI or anyone from AG Frey's office.
Nearly six months later, Bellows seems to have filed the Amazon Absentee Ballots into the memory hole. She's too busy spoon feeding jello and Geritol to her core voters, after all. She's not the only one. The entire Maine political establishment, including the taxpayer-funded newspapers, seem to have moved on from the fiasco. Investigation 101 says you conduct interviews as soon as possible, while memories are still fresh. Human memories have a way of morphing overtime.
The lack of any interviews in the immediate days and weeks following the catastrophic election blunder is a virtual guarantee that Bellows, Frey, and Maine's entire election apparatus have swept this scandal under the rug. The truth is, there is no investigation; there never was. And no one -- least of all Shenna Bellows -- wants the public to know how her office managed such a galactic screw-up. Or, perhaps they did find the culprit, they don't what the public to have answers, and what we're looking at instead is a cover-up.
The only action Bellows took in response to the Amazon Absentee Ballot was to strip UPS of the ballot distribution contract and hand a no-bid contract to a separate parcel delivery service. She never transparently explained why she called the audible. But the Amazon Absentee Ballots are only _Part One_ of this epic Bellows boo-boo. _Part Two_ is even more intriguing, especially because Bellows continues to deceive and delay about this cock-up.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/56230e59-f0d2-4f6d-b363-b342fe915ff1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)| | |
#### [Maine Secretary of State Admits Non-Citizens Registered to Vote](https://substack.com/redirect/56230e59-f0d2-4f6d-b363-b342fe915ff1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
---
| | [The Robinson Report](https://substack.com/profile/147548156-the-robinson-report)| | *
---|---|---
| August 29, 2025
| [| Read full story
---](https://substack.com/redirect/56230e59-f0d2-4f6d-b363-b342fe915ff1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
At the same time absentee ballots were _somehow_ finding their way into the wrong Amazon Prime package, we had the simultaneous scandal involving absentee ballot affidavit envelopes turning up at some Washington, D.C.-area consulting firm. Bellows refuses to tell lawmakers (or journalists) the name of the firm. That was one detail she conveniently forgot the last time she testified about it at the State House. That little detail just slipped her mind at the hearing, and then she subsequently refused to let it slip back into her mind when lawmakers and journalists followed up.
To restate it bluntly: Shenna Bellows mailed some DC area consulting firm -- perhaps it was Public Policy Partners, Harris Jones & Malone, LLC, ActBlue, or some Democrat campaign shop -- sensitive election materials, and she only confessed once the Amazon Absentee fiasco put a microscope on her election mismanagement. Yet even now, six months later, she's still refused to disclose which Democrat Party operatives got their hands on state of Maine election materials, how that happened, or how the other batch of election materials wound up in an Amazon package.
In February, Deputy Secretary of State Emily Cook (the Bellows for Governor campaign flak who's being paid by taxpayers to help run Bellows' campaign) told lawmakers on the Veterans and Legal Affairs Committee that the investigation was "still ongoing" and promised that she'd check with some unknown party to see whether she could reveal the name of the DC contractor that somehow got Maine absentee ballot envelopes. No update on that diligent work by this selfless civil servants.
Separately, we filed a Freedom of Access Act request for the name of the contractor in DC that Bellows sent absentee ballot affidavit ballots. From our reading, there's no exemption in state law that would allow them to withhold the name of Bellows' co-conspirator here. My request, submitted on Feb. 13, sought the name of the contractor and some limited instances of communication between Bellows' office and that contractor. To date, Bellows has not provided me with a "good faith" time and cost estimate for the completion of this request.
> Today I sent the following asking for an update:
> I'm writing to request an update on this FOAA request.
> It's been one month since I requested, under the Freedom of Access Act, the name of the DC-area consulting firm that the Maine SOS sent absentee ballot affidavit envelopes to, along with some limited correspondence with that firm.
> I have not received an estimate for the time or cost of this request, as state law requires.
> This request is not being handled in good faith. I understand the secretary is running for governor now and her taxpayer-funded staff have been placed in service of her political ambitions, but the law is still the law.
> Please supply the requested documents promptly.
These emails are kind of my own personal joke, because Maine's FOAA law is so poorly written that we basically have no FOAA law. It only works when government officials are honorable and ethical, and... well, we're dealing with Shenna Bellows here.

#### Six Months Later: The Amazon Absentee Cold Case
Since the single biggest election clusterf**k in state history appears to be forgotten and relegated to the archives of _The Robinson Report_ and _The Maine Wire_ , it's fair to speculate a little bit about why Bellows, Frey, and the Democrat establishment is content to forget and move on.
The Secretary of State, the very week of the scandal, settled on a right-wing conspiracy. She ignored my question at her disastrous press conference about whether she had any evidence. When another reporter asked the same question, she couldn't answer. Her accusation that I was the culprit was so thinly veiled that even the mainstream media reporters were able to understand her innuendo. But if she really believed that the Merchant of Hate had engaged in some nefarious election crime, wouldn't she be moving heaven and earth to throw me in a jail cell? Think about it: If there was a scintilla of evidence that the Amazon Absentee Ballots were part of some vast right-wing plot to gain an advantage in elections, wouldn't Gov. Janet Mills have deployed the SWAT teams?
Yet that hasn't happened.
So, why?
The most obvious explanation is: Whatever happened was part of a scheme that ultimately benefits Democrats. Perhaps those 250 absentee ballots were meant for another recipient, and perhaps we were never supposed to know about those affidavit envelopes mysteriously finding their way to a political shop in the DC area. If that were the case, then any real investigation would harm Democrats at the polls. And, if that were the case, then you'd expect Democratic officials to obliterate the Amazon Absentee Ballot scandal for our collective memory.
For the record, my leading theory is that some combination of incompetence and an accident led to the Amazon snafu. But Bellows' continued refusal to share the names of her friends in DC who got their hands on absentee envelopes... well, that does make me wonder.

Today I sent the following asking for an update: I'm writing to request an update on this FOAA request. It's been one month since I requested, under the Freedom of Access Act, the name of the DC-area consulting firm that the Maine SOS sent absentee ballot affidavit envelopes to, along with some limited correspondence with that firm. I have not received an estimate for the time or cost of this request, as state law requires. This request is not being handled in good faith. I understand the secretary is running for governor now and her taxpayer-funded staff have been placed in service of her political ambitions, but the law is still the law. Please supply the requested documents promptly. These emails are kind of my own personal joke, because Maine's FOAA law is so poorly written that we basically have no FOAA law. It only works when government officials are honorable and ethical, and... well, we're dealing with Shenna Bellows here. Subscribe to Maine's most popular political newsletter! Six Months Later: The Amazon Absentee Cold Case Since the single biggest election clusterfk in state history appears to be forgotten and relegated to the archives of The Robinson Report and The Maine Wire , it's fair to speculate a little bit about why Bellows, Frey, and the Democrat establishment is content to forget and move on. The Secretary of State, the very week of the scandal, settled on a right-wing conspiracy. She ignored my question at her disastrous press conference about whether she had any evidence. When another reporter asked the same question, she couldn't answer. Her accusation that I was the culprit was so thinly veiled that even the mainstream media reporters were able to understand her innuendo. But if she really believed that the Merchant of Hate had engaged in some nefarious election crime, wouldn't she be moving heaven and earth to throw me in a jail cell? Think about it: If there was a scintilla of evidence that the Amazon Absentee Ballots were part of some vast right-wing plot to gain an advantage in elections, wouldn't Gov. Janet Mills have deployed the SWAT teams? Yet that hasn't happened. So, why? The most obvious explanation is: Whatever happened was part of a scheme that ultimately benefits Democrats. Perhaps those 250 absentee ballots were meant for another recipient, and perhaps we were never supposed to know about those affidavit envelopes mysteriously finding their way to a political shop in the DC area. If that were the case, then any real investigation would harm Democrats at the polls. And, if that were the case, then you'd expect Democratic officials to obliterate the Amazon Absentee Ballot scandal for our collective memory. For the record, my leading theory is that some combination of incompetence and an accident led to the Amazon snafu. But Bellows' continued refusal to share the names of her friends in DC who got their hands on absentee envelopes... well, that does make me wonder. ? * You 're receiving The Robinson Report for free. Last election, one of Charlie Kirk’s full-time ballot-chasers (Mike C.) was assigned to a small neighborhood in a battleground district.
He knocked on 42 doors in one afternoon.
Most people weren’t planning to vote.
Some hadn’t voted in years.
Like all of Charlie’s ballot-chasers, Mike committed to chasing a minimum of 10 ballots every day.
By the end of early voting, Mike had helped **bank 447 ballots** from that one neighborhood.
Multiply that effort across thousands of ballot-chasers...
...and you understand how elections are won.
Charlie Kirk built this model.
It’s time to get our hands dirty again and scale it.
Turning Point PAC wants to unleash America’s ballot-chasing army (again) in key districts that will keep Republican control of the House and Senate.
**Put simply: We need more Mikes.**
More Mikes will decide the House. More Mikes will decide the Senate.
Your contribution **DIRECTLY** puts more Mikes in the field:
🟢 $50 → Sponsors **1 Mike** → 10 ballots/day 🟢 $100 → Sponsors **2 Mikes** → 20 ballots/day 🟢 $250 → Powers a **team of Mikes** → 50 ballots/day 🟢 $500 → Funds a **squad of Mikes** → 100 ballots/day 🟢 $1,000+ → **An entire platoon of Mikes!** → 200+ ballots/day
Unlike other political contributions, you know EXACTLY what you’re buying with a contribution to Turning Point PAC.
The only question is:
**[How much impact do _YOU_ want to have?](https://click.parlermailer.com/?%3D%3D)**
REMEMBER: House races are often decided by **fewer than 5,000 votes** and Senate races by **less than 1%**.
**Your contribution not only _CAN_ make a difference, you _WILL_ make a difference.**
Help us win this ground war.
For Charlie,
Tyler Bowyer
Executive DIrector
Turning Point PAC

| | | **Dear Friend,** We are officially down to the final 36 hours of this fundraising quarter—and I need your help to finish strong. **From day one, this campaign has been about three things: relationships, experience, and results.** I am a fourth-generation Lowcountry native. I have built my life, raised my family, and grown my business right here in the First District. These aren’t just talking points—they are the relationships that fuel this campaign every single day. [**DONATE NOW TO OUR CAMPAIGN**](https://VoteMarkSmith.us20.list-manage.com/track/click?u=75ca839227bb28c57ff73dffe&id=322419f369&e=d4051626af) I also bring the experience to get to work on day one. From serving on Mount Pleasant Town Council to representing you in the State House, I know how to navigate tough challenges and deliver real solutions. _And most importantly, I have a record of results._
✔️ Helped pass the largest tax cut in South Carolina history
✔️ Eliminated the income tax on military retirement

name: DNC Coalitions Engagement Team
subject: Introducing the DNC Playbook
body:
| | | | | [|
---](https://collegedems.us12.list-manage.com/track/click?u=b3a52587106e5f265f227782b&id=c3a0f4d34c&e=d6c5c7d7ec)
|
---
| | Hello Democrats!
Today, the DNC is proud to launch our inaugural Playbook: a guide for state parties and campaigns with the guidance, resources, and best practices they need to run winning organizing programs in 2026 and beyond. This moment demands an overhaul of organizing and campaign strategy: one that rewrites the structures and assumptions that define campaigns and the day-to-day work of an organizer.
Democratic campaign operatives know that we need to evolve how we organize in 2026 if we want to win and this Playbook provides guidance to inform how they do it. [**READ THE PLAYBOOK!**](https://collegedems.us12.list-manage.com/track/click?u=b3a52587106e5f265f227782b&id=07734b099c&e=d6c5c7d7ec)
---
|
---
| |
**What’s next:**
* **Share the Playbook with your networks!**[**democrats.org/playbook**](https://collegedems.us12.list-manage.com/track/click?u=b3a52587106e5f265f227782b&id=411c843656&e=d6c5c7d7ec)
* **Read the**[**Playbook**](https://collegedems.us12.list-manage.com/track/click?u=b3a52587106e5f265f227782b&id=b3768437ee&e=d6c5c7d7ec)**! The Playbook is a tool for campaign staff and operatives.**

---
| | |
**Here’s how to navigate**
* **Are you working on an organizing program in a state?** Check out the Organizing Re-Model section for inspiration for writing scripts, additional tactics to consider, and organizational structures.

* **Are you deciding what organizing tools to use for your campaign?** Check out the Technology Pilots section to view the findings from the DNC’s 2025 pilots, and see if any of those tools could be a good fit for your team.

* **Are you strategizing on how to reach key constituencies in your district?** Check out the Community Power Fellowship section to view best practices from local community organizers who have successfully organized diverse communities on the ground across the country.

* **Are you curious about what innovations took place in 2025?** Check out the Case Studies section to learn from innovative programs launched on campaigns last year.

A few notes:
* **No candidates, states, or campaigns are the same.** The Playbook provides baseline principles, templates, and guides that can be adapted to organize on any race.

* **Take from it what’s helpf** ul. Throughout the Playbook we encourage states and campaigns to take ideas that are helpful, leave what doesn’t work, and to challenge our ideas.

* **The Playbook is a living documen** t. As we test and pilot strategies, we will update the Playbook to highlight what’s working and where we can pivot.
* Have innovative ideas or work you want to share for the next Playbook? Share it HERE.

Happy Organizing!

---

---

In 1992, Notre Dame rejected my transfer application.
At the time, I thought I was living my own version of [Rudy](https://substack.com/redirect/b1a3a295-0de7-4dc8-97a2-766ae7851c74?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) -- the kid from a working-class family who outworked everyone around him and aimed higher than anyone expected. I was 17, a full-time student at Bucks County Community College, on the Dean's List and honor roll, while working four jobs: waiting tables on the graveyard shift from 11pm to 6am, messenger at the Murphy & O'Connor Law Firm (no relation), Eagles security guard on the 700 level -- where they had an actual jail inside the stadium -- and working in the Phillies' marketing department. Notre Dame didn't see it that way.
The Secretary's SitRep is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..rjwvEhII_NyLxe-n6zp2UECjq-4QurT0xGy8lQXp158?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=192627911)
Instead, I went on to thrive at King's College, one of the six universities founded by the Congregation of the Holy Cross -- the same order that founded Notre Dame.
In my senior year at King's, I applied to Notre Dame Law School and got rejected again.
The irony, three decades later, is that they've now invited me twice as a speaker.
Notre Dame is an institution that has had an incredible military history, dating back before the Civil War.
In 1842, Father Sorin's founding mission was that "graduates would go forth and be forces for good in the world." It's the connective tissue between Catholicism and military service.
World War II is when Notre Dame truly cemented its place in military history. At the time, Notre Dame was losing students to the war effort and nearly went broke: [enrollment dropped to around 750](https://substack.com/redirect/49c33d49-725a-4057-bca2-0d4720288e1e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) students. The Navy stepped in with its V-7 (and later V-12) officer training program, taught by Notre Dame faculty, and brought enrollment back up to 3,500+. They even signed a contract guaranteeing the university[ $487,711](https://substack.com/redirect/e278ff65-7c45-4b5d-b965-5d5795937c51?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to keep the lights on. By war's end, Notre Dame had produced over [10,000 commissioned naval reserve officers](https://substack.com/redirect/a5f4a8d3-9414-4df2-b4c9-4b7e8f6a00aa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
During Vietnam, when universities across the country were shutting down their ROTC programs, Father Hesburgh held the line and kept Notre Dame's open. Though he was personally against the war, he believed Notre Dame had a responsibility to send morally grounded, ethically formed officers into an inevitable reality of military conflict.
This weekend I had the honor of giving the keynote speech at Notre Dame Law School for their Veterans Law Clinic's first anniversary.
You can watch my speech [here](https://substack.com/redirect/1e736d62-f995-4540-8ff7-85bd0e3626c8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) (my remarks begin at 4:13):21)
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f1c644f5-8b11-43bb-b995-06112438823e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
You can read my full remarks below.
***
Rob [Rizzo], thank you so much for your leadership. We're very proud at West Point that he's a phenomenal graduate. He's now a second year law student here at Notre Dame, and he's just a flat out great American. So thank you so much for your continued leadership to our nation as obviously one of the key student leaders here, and I want to just thank Professor [Caleb] Stone as well for your leadership. That is a fine institution, and what you do here today, and how you built the veterans Law Clinic in just one year.
I had to say, as a proud Irish Catholic who grew up and continues to go to Mass every Sunday, speaking at Notre Dame is something that I do not take lightly. I was here with the Vice Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff [Admiral Grady] two years ago, and I was inspired to be there and to see how this campus and the student body continues to grow. It's inspiring. This is a place that I've looked up to my entire life, and these hallowed halls are revered where I come from.
I'm honored to be in this room and walked in with Senator Joe Donnelly, Notre Dame double Domer, who became the US Ambassador to the Holy See and started his public service on a Mishawaka Marion school board back in 1997 before becoming a US Congressman ten years later. In 2007, we were classmates together in Congress and co-authored the post-9/11 GI Bill, and that GI Bill has helped millions of veterans and family members across this country, including 800,000 currently attending colleges and universities across America. I also love to acknowledge Tom Mendoza, who built something extraordinary here at Notre Dame within the Mendoza Business School. When I was helping lead the Army, we brought him into the Pentagon to talk to our senior leaders, our generals, about culture and how important that is. The way Tom Mendoza thinks about culture and public-private partnerships tells you everything about what this institution produces. He's a self-made man who never stopped acting like he had something to prove, and that kind of energy matters in building great institutions here at Notre Dame and across our globe.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/eec416ee-748b-4b40-bb75-cd411f872499?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
_(With former Senator and US Ambassador to the Holy See, Joe Donnelly (D-IN); he was trolling me with this NAVY sweatshirt)_
And of course, one of your most distinguished alums sits today on the US Supreme Court: Justice Amy Coney Barrett. I'm a fan of hers and her recent opinion is a reminder to all of us that our US Constitution, the blueprint of our country, of a democracy, establishes three co-equal branches of government.
There's a famous line from Shakespeare's _Henry VI, Part Two_ : "The first thing we do, let's kill all the lawyers." The man who says it is a henchman to a rebel leader trying to seize power. He knows exactly what stands in his way: intelligent lawyers, the people who would show up and defend the citizens they are about to abuse. The people who want to consolidate power at the expense of ordinary citizens have always known that lawyers are the obstacle.
And that's why being here today at this conference, entitled "Service Members in Society: Veterans as Stewards of the Public Good," is so important. Because public service means being a steward of the public good. The question that I pose, especially to the young law students here, is whether you're willing to become that obstacle. Are you willing to be the person someone calls when they have nowhere else to turn? Skilled lawyers are the ultimate problem solvers. You're becoming the person in the room with the strength of mind to stand between ordinary people and the forces that would rather they didn't know their rights. And veteran lawyers have a warrior mindset that distinguishes them from their peers.
I was blessed to be commissioned as a US Army officer at King's College. It's one of the six colleges and universities across America that were founded by the Congregation of the Holy Cross. I was a 1996 graduate, and that same commissioning year at the University of Notre Dame was a young cadet who became a second lieutenant named Ken Heckle. Years later, after we graduated and commissioned in 1996, Ken and I served at the same time in the 82nd Airborne Division. We were there during a time when the war in Iraq began. We both served in combat. We were both professors later on at West Point, and then after my time in the Pentagon as Acting Secretary of the Army, Ken and I were both senior leaders at the United States Military Academy at West Point. Ken is my brother paratrooper, and he now leads the Sergeant John F. Crowley Office of Military and Veterans Affairs. Ken and I share a lot of things in service, but it is that mentality of what the Bible talks about, _selfless service,_ that drives us both and so many others in this room.
Ladies and gentlemen, I grew up in Northeast Philadelphia in a working-class family, and the kind of neighborhood where people didn't have lawyers on speed dial. On weekends in high school, I'd work the graveyard shift waiting tables at Perkins Family Restaurant, and during the day, I worked security at the old Veterans Stadium on the 700 level, where the Philadelphia Eagles played. If you know anything about Eagles sports fans and the old Veterans Stadium -- where we had a jail in the stadium -- you understood that this was essentially a graduate seminar in conflict resolution. I maintain that that job prepared me more for war and the invasion of Iraq in 2003 than anything else in my life. At that time, I was only 125 pounds and had to deal with some of the rowdiest, beer-fueled brawls you could have possibly imagined.
But I come from a long line of veterans -- I'm a third-generation veteran, so perhaps I seemed destined for a military career. My grandfather served in World War II in the US Navy in the Pacific. My father served during Vietnam, Navy enlisted. My two uncles were in the Army, both Vietnam veterans. One of them, my Uncle Billy, served in Vietnam with the 101st Airborne and then became a paratrooper in the 82nd Airborne Division, and he would influence my decision to follow in his footsteps. And then my brother, JJ Murphy, was in the Air Force with two deployments after 9/11. That's not even everyone in my family that served.
But I say that because my career in service was not in a straight line. I started my academic career at 17 at Bucks County Community College before transferring to King's College. And it's also when I decided at 19 to join the Army ROTC program, partially because my roommate was joining and we found out you could get $150 paid a month by taking military science classes and joining the program. But despite coming from a military family, I shockingly didn't know much about military life. Couldn't tell you the difference between an officer and enlisted, or whether a captain outranked a lieutenant, or how to earn a commission as an officer, which you can do through ROTC, a service academy, or in the Army through Officer Candidate School.
I delayed after being commissioned my active duty service so I could attend law school at Widener University, Commonwealth School of Law in Harrisburg, Pennsylvania. And that decision was one that changed everything, though I couldn't have told you that at the time. The combination of law and military service became two of the linchpins that set me on my path. In law school, I became the president of the St. Thomas More Society, and I was a student clinic leader at our legal clinic, the Harrisburg Civil Law Clinic. I got my first real taste of law and public interest. We set up a free legal clinic outside of the Harrisburg clinic at the St. Francis Soup Kitchen in downtown Harrisburg. And that small decision to go where the people most in need are has stayed with me for over 30 years.
I learned that in part from one of the presidents of King's College, Father Tom O'Hara. He was on the board here at Notre Dame. He was a professor when I knew him when I was a student at King's College, and he went on sabbatical back in 1993 to do mission work in Africa, then came back to serve as our president. He modeled to me what it looks like to put service first. And I gave my first real public speech when I was at King's when I was at lectern at our local Sunday night masses.
When I graduated from law school, I never imagined that four years later I would be prosecuting terrorists in the Supreme Court of Iraq under their 1967 Iraqi criminal code. That wasn't exactly a course we learned in law school, but I had to learn a legal system in a language I didn't speak, in a country at war, in order to make justice happen trying one of the first cases in the Supreme Court of Iraq, known as the Central Criminal Court of Iraq. But the law and the justice system was one of the only legitimate tools that we had.
There's a unique overlap between military service and law that doesn't get examined enough. Both institutions ask you to put aside your personal interest and honor something larger than yourself. Both operate through codes and procedure. In fact, our motto in the Army JAG Corps is "soldiers first, lawyers always." And that's why so many veterans like Robert Rizzo and many of you in this room find that law is a natural continuation of that service.
History is filled with examples. Alexander Hamilton served as Washington's top military aide before becoming one of the most consequential lawyers in our young republic. Oliver Wendell Holmes Jr. was wounded three times in the Civil War before becoming one of the most influential Supreme Court justices in American history. Abraham Lincoln served in the Illinois militia before becoming a self-taught lawyer and one of the most formidable trial attorneys of his era. Gerald Ford served in the Navy before attending Michigan Law. There's a reason why military leaders make great legal minds. The pattern is not a coincidence.
Military service teaches you that rules matter, that without them, power fills the vacuum and the wrong people suffer first. It teaches you to stay calm when the stakes are highest, to think clearly when everything is loud and urgent and nothing is certain. These are not just soldierly values. They are exactly what a courtroom demands, what a client in crisis deserves. And I found that out firsthand after graduating law school when I entered the Army JAG Corps, which was founded by George Washington back in 1775, making it the largest and oldest law firm in our country.
I later joined the faculty at West Point, where I taught constitutional and military law at age 27 as the youngest professor at that time at West Point. I taught with great leaders -- people like Captain Tom Rooney, who became a member of Congress with me. My best friend in the Army, my best friend at West Point, is my best friend in Congress -- and yet we were from two different political parties.
So let me now bring this back to you. In poll after poll, American military veterans rank among the most trusted groups in public life. Lawyers, on the other hand... well, you know the jokes about lawyers. But the point is that veteran lawyers occupy a space at the intersection of credibility and expertise that this country desperately needs more of right now, especially in public service. At a time when trust in institutions is fragile and polarization is high, veterans have an opportunity to restore trust. And because you're sitting here, you've already demonstrated a willingness to put country before self.
The lawyers who go into public defender offices, legal aid organizations like this Veterans Law Clinic, federal agencies, state attorneys general offices -- they are doing some of the most consequential legal work in this country. They are in courtrooms every day where the stakes are not a contract dispute, but someone's freedom, someone's family, someone's ability to stay in the country they've built their entire life in. The pay is not what it is in big law firms. Nobody's going to write a profile of you in a legal trade publication. But the work is real in a way that is genuinely hard to replicate, and the skills you build are extraordinary.

Public service makes you a better lawyer, and more importantly, makes you the kind of lawyer this country actually needs right now.
I see this in my work today on the advisory board for the Legal Services Corporation, which funds free legal clinics across the country -- a board I've now served on for nine years. The chair of the Legal Services Corporation is John Levi, a top partner at the Sidley Austin law firm. John Levi has an uncanny knack for attracting talent. His father was the Attorney General, and the president of the University of Chicago. John Levi and I became friends when I was a young congressman. He, before my time, hired a young woman from Harvard Law School named Michelle Robinson. The next year, he hired a young Harvard law student named Barack Obama.
What the Legal Services Corporation does is provide funding for free legal aid clinics across the country. And what you see when you look at how that system actually operates -- and those in this clinic know this -- is that there are effectively two justice systems in America: one for people who can afford a lawyer, and one for everybody else. And that's where many of you in this room, at this clinic, bridge the gap for our veterans. It's a daily reality for millions of people whose legal problems are completely solvable with competent representation and completely devastating without it.
The model I lived at that St. Francis Soup Kitchen in downtown Harrisburg is to go where people are, rather than wait for them to find you. That's what the Legal Services Corporation is trying to institutionalize at scale across this country. It's hard work, but it's deeply rewarding. It's what we're celebrating today, on the one-year anniversary of the Veterans Law Clinic here at the University of Notre Dame Law School.
So I leave you with this: carry that thread of service forward. Carry it into every space where power intersects with responsibility, because the measure of a life in service is not the uniform you once wore. It's in the integrity you bring to everything that follows. Thank you very much.

With Holy Week upon us, we're all called to be a force for good.
Wishing you a happy Easter.

## Join the Vote No Rally with Governor Youngkin & Congressman McGuire! 🇺🇸

Virginia is at a crossroads. Join us in Lynchburg to help us get out the vote.

* When: April 11, 2026 | 9:00 AM - 11:00 AM
* Where: Bella Rose, 1220 Graves Mill Rd, Lynchburg, VA
* Special Guest: Governor Glenn Youngkin
* Featured Speakers: Sen. Mark Peake, Sen. Luther Ciphers, and Del. Wendell Walker

Get Involved: Learn the latest on redistricting and how you can help through door knocking, phone banking, or outreach. Supported by Turning Point Action and The Family Foundation. Make a plan to knock doors with us after the rally. Get involved, VOTE NO, and please tell a friend.
If you want to join Team McGuire and help us help Trump Save America, please contact Ramona Christian at ramona@mcguireva.com or call her at 434 391 4546.

I'm proud to announce that Team McGuire has successfully passed two critical bills through the House in just three weeks.
The Wintergreen Emergency Egress Act This one is a massive win for public safety. For 25 years, this issue remained unsolved, with six different past congressional offices in the 5th attempting to find a fix. When my team and I learned of this issue in my district last August, we rolled up our sleeves and got to work. By working across the aisle and staying focused on results, we did the "impossible" and passed this bill through the House in just six months with bipartisan support.
The Make the District of Columbia Safe and Beautiful Act In addition to the Wintergreen Emergency Egress Act, my bill to revitalize and secure our nation's capital has officially passed. This bill codifies President Trumps Executive Order. Constituents from my district travel to DC everyday for work and leisure. We are committed to ensuring that the heart of our Republic, our nation's Capitol, is a safe, clean, and welcoming place for every American who visits.
The Bottom Line Results Matter: Whether it's a decades-old safety concern at Wintergreen or the safety of our people when they visit our capitol, we are proving that with the right work ethic and a commitment to working as a team for success, we can get Washington working again. Thank you for your continued support as we keep fighting for you!

My bill to create an emergency egress at Wintergreen Ski Resort passed the House. I thought about starting this post off with a joke ("Just what the world needs right now, another podcast"), but I'm actually really excited about this project, so I'm just going to be earnest. Today, three friends and I are launching a new podcast, sponsored by _The Nation_ , to help you fight back against fascism.
You can listen to the first episode here:
_[Fighting Fascism](https://substack.com/redirect/66ac13a8-4321-44ef-8c65-55dc0160ae61?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_[ on Apple Podcasts](https://substack.com/redirect/66ac13a8-4321-44ef-8c65-55dc0160ae61?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
_[Fighting Fascism](https://substack.com/redirect/800c44ad-277e-4f42-a752-50aa72155f3f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_[ on Spotify](https://substack.com/redirect/800c44ad-277e-4f42-a752-50aa72155f3f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
We're in a moment that demands not just outrage, but strategy. So this is a show that will look hard at past and present fascist movements, the conditions that enabled them, and--crucially--the resistance movements that defeated them.
Each week, my friends Matt DaSilva, Jonathan Smucker, and I (with the help of our producer, Nik Damants) will sit down with historians, strategists, and activists. We'll be looking both forward and backward: For example, next week we're talking with Morris Katz, the lead strategist for Zohran Mamdani's campaign, on why the Democratic Party keeps fumbling and how to make it stop; after that we'll interview Eric Rauchway, a leading expert on FDR--America's original antifascist--on what Roosevelt's New Deal coalition can teach us about winning.
Today's episode features Astra Taylor, author of _End Times Fascism_ , and Mark Bray, author of _Antifa: The Anti-Fascist Handbook_ , who joined us for a big picture conversation about what it means to fight fascism in this historical moment. We talked about popular resistance to ICE, tensions between "radical" and "normie" mobilization, how much we all hate AI, and why it shouldn't actually be _that_ hard to build a majoritarian coalition around the idea that a few dozen creepy billionaires shouldn't own literally everything on the planet. I really think you'll enjoy the conversation, and hope you'll check it __ out!
And, if I can be so bold as to ask a personal favor: I'd be grateful if you could take five seconds to give the show a rating on your podcast app ([Apple](https://substack.com/redirect/66ac13a8-4321-44ef-8c65-55dc0160ae61?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) or [Spotify](https://substack.com/redirect/d3c7d878-6467-4b18-b7ad-8f763e58dbb8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)). **Truly, it would mean a lot to me, as this has a big effect on whether people will find the podcast on their feed.**
Thanks a million! Oh, and here are a few short clips from today's episode if you want to get a taste of the discussion:
Astra on Big Tech
[](https://substack.com/redirect/dab9cdb6-5012-4d4a-868f-a760d6b16a7a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Mark on antifascism and art
[](https://substack.com/redirect/783b1190-98f1-4232-ba7c-bf35791d2555?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Me on billionaires
[](https://substack.com/redirect/f2f83400-b0d3-413e-8db2-1fd950885565?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Please consider subscribing, and you can also follow _Fighting Fascism_ on [Twitter](https://substack.com/redirect/b96477c0-c4f2-4899-a0a2-df09a297d8c5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [Bluesky](https://substack.com/redirect/d38459e8-646d-4bff-a67d-d8eb7d574af2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and [Instagram](https://substack.com/redirect/263c7d0e-b876-4388-a08c-e97e7827c046?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Thanks again!

TSA workers sold plasma while Tran played politics. Q1 deadline is tomorrow.
**Friend,**
While Derek Tran was playing politics in Washington, TSA agents here in Southern California were selling their blood plasma just to pay for gas.
Not a metaphor. Not a talking point.
Real people. Real needles. Real desperation.
The shutdown that froze their paychecks started February 14th. Over 300 TSA officers quit. Some drove for DoorDash between shifts. Others lined up at plasma centers to cover their rent.
Derek Tran voted against the funding that would have paid them.
He called it a stand against "drastic cuts." But those TSA officers — essential workers, security screeners, your neighbors — they were the ones paying the price for his political stand.
I know what it's like to have nothing.
My dad walked off a boat in Huntington Beach in 1987 with $20 in his pocket. He didn't have a congressman fighting for him. He didn't have a safety net. He had grit, and the belief that this country was worth it.
Those TSA workers believed the same thing. They showed up every single day — unpaid — because they took an oath to keep Americans safe.
Derek Tran left them hanging.
I won't.

Peter, I want to tell you about a fight that does not get nearly enough attention. For years, vaccine manufacturers have had a special legal shield that protects them from being sued when their products cause harm. No other major industry gets this kind of treatment. Not auto manufacturers. Not food companies. Not anyone. **If your family is hurt, you deserve the right to hold powerful corporations accountable. That is a principle every American should agree on.** That is why I introduced the End the Vaccine Carve Out Act. It removes this special protection and puts vaccine makers under the same legal standards as everyone else. This is not a partisan issue. Republicans, Democrats, and Independents overwhelmingly agree that no corporation should be above the law. clean_body: If your family is hurt, you deserve the right to hold powerful corporations accountable. | | | | Please see a special message from our sponsor. If you would like to unsubscribe, visit this Peter, I want to tell you about a fight that does not get nearly enough attention. For years, vaccine manufacturers have had a special legal shield that protects them from being sued when their products cause harm. No other major industry gets this kind of treatment. Not auto manufacturers. Not food companies. Not anyone. If your family is hurt, you deserve the right to hold powerful corporations accountable. That is a principle every American should agree on. That is why I introduced the End the Vaccine Carve Out Act. It removes this special protection and puts vaccine makers under the same legal standards as everyone else. This is not a partisan issue. Republicans, Democrats, and Independents overwhelmingly agree that no corporation should be above the law. Polls show this is the most popular vaccine safety reform Congress could pursue. But Big Pharma and their army of lobbyists are spending millions to kill this bill and keep their special treatment. The political class listens to lobbyists. I listen to the people. Your support right now helps me keep fighting for accountability against some of the most powerful interests in Washington. In liberty, Rand Paul | | | | | | Paid for by Rand Paul for Senate | | P.O. | | | | High school dropout. Waffle House waitress. First woman to graduate from The Citadel. Single mom. Fighter.

Nancy Mace wasn’t born into power. She worked for every inch of ground she’s gained.

At 17, she dropped out of high school and took a job slinging hash browns at Waffle House to survive. No silver spoon. No Ivy League connections. Just grit, grace, and a whole lot of graveyard shifts.

By the grace of God, she turned that struggle into a story no politician can touch. She made history as the first woman to graduate from The Citadel, South Carolina’s legendary military college. She built her own business. She raised two kids on her own. And when the Left came for everything she believed in, she stood her ground. Now, she’s running for Governor of South Carolina.

Nancy Mace is a battle-tested conservative who’s walked through fire and come out swinging. In Congress, she’s been one of President Trump’s fiercest allies, fighting to secure our border, protect our daughters, and stop the Left’s sick agenda dead in its tracks.

She’s not here to make friends. She’s here to make history.

Nancy is fighting to:

* Eliminate South Carolina’s Income Tax—the highest in the Southeast

* Prosecute violent criminals and pedophiles with zero leniency

* Crack down on sanctuary sheriffs who let illegal aliens roam free

* Defund radical public universities that indoctrinate, not educate

* Reform education so students learn how to think—not what to think

* Work hand-in-hand with President Trump to put South Carolina FIRST

Through every hardship, Nancy never gave up. And now she’s ready to do what she’s always done: roll up her sleeves, take the heat, and lead from the front.

South Carolina is worth fighting for. And Nancy Mace is just getting started.

Dear Peter,
If we’re serious about winning back the House in 2026, we need to be honest about how we do it.
We don’t win by running the same playbook with the same candidates funded by the same big donors.
We win by lifting up working-class candidates who know what it means to live paycheck to paycheck, and who aren’t owned by corporate PACs or billionaire interests.
That’s why I’m proud to endorse Paul Nolley for Congress in Illinois’ 16th District.
Before I tell you more, can you split a contribution today between my campaign and Paul Nolley’s to help us build the kind of movement that can win in 2026? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rk-paul-nolley-fundraising-split?refcode=20260330]
DONATE >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rk-paul-nolley-fundraising-split?refcode=20260330]
Paul isn’t a career politician.
He grew up in Rockford, working at a racetrack, in food service, retail, and farm fields, doing the kinds of jobs that keep this country running but are too often ignored in Washington.
Today, he’s helping expand union careers and apprenticeship programs across northwest Illinois, creating real pathways for working people to get ahead.
And just like me, he’s not taking a dime from corporate PACs or big-money lobbyists.
If we’re going to flip the House in 2026, it’s going to take early investment in grassroots campaigns like this one.

Thank you for your support, your activism, and everything that you do.
In solidarity,

Peter,

I’m excited to share a major win for our community: the Montgomery County Council has become the first jurisdiction to join the Metropolitan Washington Council of Governments (COG) Local Food Procurement Challenge.

I launched this initiative and spearheaded this resolution to set us on a path to strengthen local food systems, support small farmers, and make Montgomery County more resilient. By investing in local farms and regional food networks, we're ensuring better food access, boosting our economy, and reducing our environmental impact.

But this is just the beginning. I’m running for County Executive to keep leading and making progress on these critical issues. I launched this initiative and spearheaded this resolution to set us on a path to strengthen local food systems, support small farmers, and make Montgomery County more resilient. By investing in local farms and regional food networks, we're ensuring better food access, boosting our economy, and reducing our environmental impact. But this is just the beginning. I’m running for County Executive to keep leading and making progress on these critical issues. As we continue our series on the 14 Signs of Fascism, we arrive at a particularly concerning indicator: **Religion and Government are Intertwined.** In a healthy democracy, the separation of church and state protects the freedom of all. However, in a burgeoning autocracy, government leaders use religion as a powerful political tool. By wrapping policy in the cloak of divinity, leaders can manipulate public opinion, casting their political opponents not just as wrong, but as evil. This tactic bypasses rational debate and uses personal faith to shield government actions from secular scrutiny. We see this clearly in the current political climate. Under the Trump administration, the "Project 2025" blueprint has transitioned from a plan to a reality, aiming to infuse every federal agency with biblical principles. >From the creation of the White House Faith Office to the Task Force to Eradicate Anti-Christian Bias, the state is no longer a neutral arbiter. Instead, religious rhetoric is used to justify the rollback of reproductive rights, the erasure of LGBTQ+ protections, and the redirection of public tax dollars to sectarian private schools. When the government claims to be doing "God’s work," it suggests that any opposition is not just a disagreement, but a sin against the nation. When the line between the pulpit and the podium blurs, the rights of the minority are often the first to go. **At Local Democracy Project, we recruit, train, and support candidates at the state and local level who will protect the separation of church and state. Our mission is to keep our democracy healthy, inclusive, and strictly secular.** [**Your support helps us place defenders of democracy in school boards and city councils across the country. clean_body: | | | Sign #8: No separation between church and state. As we continue our series on the 14 Signs of Fascism, we arrive at a particularly concerning indicator: Religion and Government are Intertwined. In a healthy democracy, the separation of church and state protects the freedom of all. However, in a burgeoning autocracy, government leaders use religion as a powerful political tool. By wrapping policy in the cloak of divinity, leaders can manipulate public opinion, casting their political opponents not just as wrong, but as evil. This tactic bypasses rational debate and uses personal faith to shield government actions from secular scrutiny. We see this clearly in the current political climate. Under the Trump administration, the "Project 2025" blueprint has transitioned from a plan to a reality, aiming to infuse every federal agency with biblical principles. >From the creation of the White House Faith Office to the Task Force to Eradicate Anti-Christian Bias, the state is no longer a neutral arbiter. Instead, religious rhetoric is used to justify the rollback of reproductive rights, the erasure of LGBTQ+ protections, and the redirection of public tax dollars to sectarian private schools. When the government claims to be doing "God’s work," it suggests that any opposition is not just a disagreement, but a sin against the nation. When the line between the pulpit and the podium blurs, the rights of the minority are often the first to go. At Local Democracy Project, we recruit, train, and support candidates at the state and local level who will protect the separation of church and state. Our mission is to keep our democracy healthy, inclusive, and strictly secular.
