* * *
So Axios had a story this weekend about how a bunch of DC-based Democratic strategists think Democrats have to run "a straight, white, Christian man" in 2028 to win the presidency. And this is exactly the kind of lazy analysis you get from a lot of the DC consulting class that drives me absolutely up a wall.
I want to take a moment to explain my position, because I think very differently than a lot of other strategists in the party.
Up front: sexism, racism, homophobia, anti-Semitism, Islamophobia--these things are real. It is harder for a person of color or a woman to get elected president of the United States. Just look at the track record. That part is obvious.
But my rebuttal isn't that those things don't exist. It's that there's something deeper going on. And if we don't understand that, we're going to keep misdiagnosing why we lose.
There are a lot of people in politics--Democrat and Republican--who will jump through every mental hoop imaginable to avoid taking responsibility when their campaigns lose. They don't stop to reflect on what they contributed to the loss. Instead, they blame the voters.
I've met plenty of people in DC who sneer at voters who don't support their candidates. It happens in both parties, and it drives me crazy.
When Kamala Harris lost in 2024, I wasn't on the campaign. But on election night, I went to bed early because it was clear there weren't enough votes in Pennsylvania for her to win. The next morning, I locked myself in a room with a whiteboard for about an hour and a half and wrote down everything I could think of that contributed to the loss--because I wanted to be part of the solution.
And I started with what I could control: myself.
I can't control voters. I can't control the media. I can't control campaigns I'm not on (hell, most of the time I can't control campaigns I am on.) But I can control what I do.
So I made a list of what I wish I'd done differently. I wish we had handled "White Dudes for Harris" differently. I wish I had spoken out more about my concerns regarding Joe Biden's health and age. I didn't do that. And a lot of us in the Democratic Party didn't either. I think that haunts many of us.
I also wasn't very public for most of those four years. Changing that is part of why I became a content creator. I started thinking more critically about how I advise clients and how I could improve. I went down deep rabbit holes--YouTube, the manosphere, how everyday Americans actually experience the economy, and other spaces--to better understand the environment we're operating in.
I'm a better consultant today than I was two years ago.
But a lot of people in this space don't want to do that kind of self-reflection. And that's how you end up with stories like this Axios piece--"It has to be a white guy"--which is really just an implicit way of shifting blame onto Kamala Harris, reducing the loss to the fact that she's a Black woman.
And while I'm absolutely certain Kamala Harris has experienced racism and sexism (I've seen firsthand the kind of bigotry that gets directed at candidates in these races--especially at Kamala.) I'm not convinced that's the primary reason she lost. I'm just not. If you changed only her race and gender, I think she still would have lost given the state of the economy and the perception of the broader Democratic Party after the Biden debate.
And as long as we keep defaulting to "run the safest white guy we can find," we're going to keep reinforcing the same dynamics we claim to want to change.
You have to be pragmatic. Of course you do. But if pragmatism just becomes an excuse to avoid risk, nothing actually changes.
So I need some of these consultants--many of whom are very good at their jobs and will be working on 2028 campaigns--to look in the mirror and ask: Were my ads good? Were my strategies sound? Was my messaging effective? Did I understand the race correctly? What mistakes did I make? How did I contribute?
Those are the questions that matter.
Instead, people are blaming voters--and, frankly, blaming Kamala Harris, who ran an imperfect but Herculean campaign that likely prevented a much worse outcome for Democrats.
This excuse-driven culture has to stop. And to be clear, I'm not talking about every individual. I'm sure someone will read this and think I'm attacking them personally--I'm not. But as a party, we have a habit of blaming everyone except ourselves.
Look at 2016. After Hillary Clinton lost, there was a massive blame game--James Comey's letter and Russian interference. Both of those things are real. But so were the strategic mistakes. A lot of people needed to take a hard look in the mirror, and many didn't, which is how we got Trump again.
It's not either/or. You can acknowledge real structural challenges and still take responsibility for your own decisions. In fact, you have to. That's how you get better--and how the candidates you work with get better.

* * *
Second, there's an identity politics angle here. For a long time, Democrats have believed they can carve up the electorate into constituencies and win through subtraction. That's not how this works.
There's been a tendency to organize campaigns around identity-based groupings--"we'll bring in this group, message to that group"--and that approach was clearly present in Kamala Harris's campaign and the broader Democratic Party. I say that as a co-founder of White Dudes for Harris. We were part of that.
At the time, it made sense in context, and there's nothing wrong with celebrating people's backgrounds or cultures. But we have to make sure everyone feels included--and more importantly, we have to recognize that identity alone isn't what wins elections. It's a piece of the puzzle, but it can't be the whole strategy.
The candidate who wins isn't going to be some mythological straight white male. We can't rebuild Bill Clinton from 1992 in the aggregate (although a lot of consultants are going to try in 2028.) It's going to be someone who feels real.
At a time when most Americans don't believe politicians are looking out for them, people are searching for someone who seems like they'll actually fight on their behalf.
Whether you like Trump or not, that's what he represents to a lot of voters. Yes, he's betrayed that trust--and that's why his approval is sinking like a rock--but the appeal was never about identity alone. It was about perceived authenticity.
That's the lesson.
And part of what gets missed in all of this is class. Most voters aren't walking around thinking about politics in terms of identity; they're thinking about whether they can afford their life. Groceries, rent, bills, stability. If you're not connecting on that level, none of the rest of it matters.
It's the same kind of surface-level analysis showing up in other parts of this conversation, too. There's another story this week about how Democrats need to run "hot" candidates--which is another piece of reductive analysis. Maybe it helps in the margins, but that's not what moves votes. And it's not the point. The point is connection. Can you talk like a normal person? Can you cut through the scripted, poll-tested DC language? Because a lot of these candidates sound like they were built in a think tank lab, and voters can feel that.
Authenticity matters more.
And history backs this up. After Democrats lost to George W. Bush in 2004, very few people would have said Barack _Hussein_ Obama was the ideal candidate for 2008. But he was--and he went on to win a historic landslide and deliver 60 Senate seats.
That kind of outcome is still possible.
But only if we're willing to do the work.
Have a real primary in 2028. Let it be messy. Let the strongest candidates rise, regardless of gender, race, and religion. Don't try to pre-select the answer based on some consultant-driven theory. Don't discount people based on identity.
Let AOC compete. Let Gretchen Whitmer compete. Let Pete Buttigieg compete. Let Josh Shapiro and JB Pritzker compete. Let them make their case to the American people and let them decide.
They're already some of the most well-liked politicians in the country. Trust the voters to decide.
If we move away from this lazy, reductive thinking--and if we start taking real responsibility for the strategies we deploy--I think Democrats can actually win big over many elections to come.

It's a piece of the puzzle, but it can't be the whole strategy. The candidate who wins isn't going to be some mythological straight white male. We can't rebuild Bill Clinton from 1992 in the aggregate (although a lot of consultants are going to try in 2028.) It's going to be someone who feels real. At a time when most Americans don't believe politicians are looking out for them, people are searching for someone who seems like they'll actually fight on their behalf. Whether you like Trump or not, that's what he represents to a lot of voters. Yes, he's betrayed that trust--and that's why his approval is sinking like a rock--but the appeal was never about identity alone. It was about perceived authenticity. That's the lesson. And part of what gets missed in all of this is class. Most voters aren't walking around thinking about politics in terms of identity; they're thinking about whether they can afford their life. Groceries, rent, bills, stability. If you're not connecting on that level, none of the rest of it matters. It's the same kind of surface-level analysis showing up in other parts of this conversation, too. There's another story this week about how Democrats need to run "hot" candidates--which is another piece of reductive analysis. Maybe it helps in the margins, but that's not what moves votes. And it's not the point. The point is connection. Can you talk like a normal person? Can you cut through the scripted, poll-tested DC language? Because a lot of these candidates sound like they were built in a think tank lab, and voters can feel that. Authenticity matters more. And history backs this up. After Democrats lost to George W. Bush in 2004, very few people would have said Barack Hussein Obama was the ideal candidate for 2008. But he was--and he went on to win a historic landslide and deliver 60 Senate seats. That kind of outcome is still possible. But only if we're willing to do the work. Have a real primary in 2028. Let it be messy. Let the strongest candidates rise, regardless of gender, race, and religion. Don't try to pre-select the answer based on some consultant-driven theory. Don't discount people based on identity. Let AOC compete. Let Gretchen Whitmer compete. Let Pete Buttigieg compete. Let Josh Shapiro and JB Pritzker compete. Let them make their case to the American people and let them decide. They're already some of the most well-liked politicians in the country. Trust the voters to decide. If we move away from this lazy, reductive thinking--and if we start taking real responsibility for the strategies we deploy--I think Democrats can actually win big over many elections to come. Mike Nellis is a Democratic strategist and entrepreneur who has raised over $1 billion for Democratic campaigns and causes. | | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. Hi there, friends, it’s Kalliana — Sue’s campaign manager — checking in with a quick update from the road.

Over the past few weeks, we’ve been all over Rhode Island with Sue. Living rooms, community events, neighborhood meetups, you name it! We’ve been having real conversations about what people want from their government.

And there’s one question that keeps coming up: _Why are you running for Lieutenant Governor?_

Totally fair. A lot of people aren’t sure what the role really does — or what it _could_ do. But if you know anything about Sue, you know she’s not afraid to roll her sleeves up and do the work.

That’s why Sue is running to make this office what it *should* be. She wants the LG’s office to be somewhere that folks can show up to get help on the issues that need more attention. She wants to push for real solutions on affordability, housing, and climate resilience, and make state government feel a lot more accessible and responsive.

In other words, she wants to be the same kind of leader she’s always been, just from a position with the opportunity to help even more Rhode Islanders.

**And I can tell you firsthand, she is not afraid of the kinds of honest conversations that must be had in order to make folks’ lives better. That’s why I know she’s the best choice for our next LG.**

But here’s the behind-the-scenes reality:

All of this — the travel, the organizing, the events, the team we’re building to keep showing up across the state — takes resources.

We’re coming up on our first end-of-quarter fundraising deadline of 2026, and we’re still working to raise an additional $8,000 before midnight on March 31. This public filing shows folks that we’re either serious about winning or we’re just background noise.

**By Wendy M. Yurgo**
Grapevine, Texas - There are moments when you realize you are not just watching a speech, you are watching history.
That is what this was.
When Crown Prince Reza Pahlavi took the stage at CPAC 2026, the room did not respond politely. It erupted. Iranian flags everywhere, people on their feet, chants breaking out again and again. Javid Shah. Reza Pahlavi. USA.
This was not a crowd listening. This was a crowd that already knew.
What he delivered was not political theater. It was clarity.
The Islamic Republic is weaker than it has been in decades, and Pahlavi said it directly. This regime is not holding together because it is strong. It is holding together because it is violent.
He described what he said was a brutal crackdown across Iran, protests crushed, entire cities locked down, and the internet repeatedly shut off so the world cannot see what is happening in real time.
And then he went further...

He said regime forces have gone into hospitals and killed wounded protesters in their beds. He spoke about doctors and nurses being tortured for treating them, about hospitals no longer functioning as places of care but as places where the regime finishes what it started in the streets.
He described what he said were staggering numbers, more than 40,000 Iranians killed and hundreds of thousands injured, and he did not present those numbers as distant statistics but as a reality unfolding inside a country that has turned on its own people.
He spoke about families walking into morgues and finding nothing, their children gone, no names, no records, only rows of bodies left unidentified. He described what he said were stacks of the dead, left there deliberately, forcing families to search through them by hand, looking for someone they loved, not knowing if they would find them or if they had already been taken and buried without a trace. Mothers, fathers, children, entire families left to carry a grief that offers no closure. He made clear this was not just brutality, it was designed to break the living.
"There is a sea of blood between the people and the regime," he said.
The room went quiet when he said it, because everyone understood exactly what he meant.
He laid out what is happening inside Iran without hesitation, a country collapsing under economic pressure, a regime losing control, internal fractures growing, and a system now trying to survive through fear alone.
Even the appearance of stability is cracking. Talk of succession, including the possible rise of Mojtaba Khamenei, is not strength, it is desperation, a regime trying to pass power through bloodlines because it has lost the people.
That is not stability. That is the end.
And that is where the shift happens.
For decades, the conversation has been about managing Iran, containing Iran, negotiating with Iran. Crown Prince Pahlavi made something very clear, this is no longer about managing the regime.
This is about ending it.

"A free Iran is not a fantasy. A free Iran is within reach."
He laid out what that future looks like, no more nuclear threats, no more terrorism, no more hostage taking, no more closing the Strait of Hormuz, no more blackmailing the global economy. A country that engages with the world instead of threatening it, a country that could normalize relations with the United States and Israel, a country that could become a stabilizing force instead of a destabilizing one, and a country with an educated population ready to rebuild and reenter the global economy in a serious way.
"Can you imagine Iran going from Death to America to God bless America?" he asked.
The crowd did not hesitate.
Pahlavi credited President Trump for creating what he described as a real window for change, but he was just as clear about the danger ahead. You do not leave a rump of this regime in place, and you do not negotiate with remnants and expect a different outcome. Any attempt to preserve pieces of the system will only give it time to regroup.
The system itself has to go.
And he made something else just as clear. This will not be handed to the Iranian people. It must be taken back.
He urged the United States to stand with them and pave the way so the Iranian people can finish the job, but not to control the outcome. This is their country, their fight, their future.
It is up to the Iranian people to take back their country.
He called for unity, for a real transition, for a referendum, for a new constitution, and for free elections. He sent a direct message to those still serving the regime, stand with the people, not the system that is killing them.
By the time he left the stage, something had changed.
His speech ran longer than expected, not because he lost the room, but because the room would not let him finish. The audience stood again and again.
This was no longer theoretical.
From that room, it felt real.
Not someday.
Now.
A free Iran is no longer a distant idea. It is a window, and for the first time in a long time, it feels like it could actually open.

He described what he said were stacks of the dead, left there deliberately, forcing families to search through them by hand, looking for someone they loved, not knowing if they would find them or if they had already been taken and buried without a trace. "There is a sea of blood between the people and the regime," he said. The room went quiet when he said it, because everyone understood exactly what he meant. April 24–26, 2026 | Legacy Center Resort & Spa | San Diego, California

The Autism Health Summit is just 3 weeks away, and we are excited to welcome our community for three powerful days of education, connection, and collaboration. As our flagship educational event, the Summit brings together leading voices in research, medicine, advocacy, and integrative health. This annual gathering is designed for parents, practitioners, researchers, and advocates seeking deeper insight into autism and neurological health from a whole-body, whole-family perspective.

We are honored to host an extraordinary lineup of speakers, including Aaron Siri, Del Bigtree, Dr. Toby Rogers, Dr. Sabine Hazan, Dr. Dayan Goodenowe, Ed Clay, and many more respected experts and thought leaders. Together, they will explore emerging research, clinical insights, environmental factors, and practical strategies that families and professionals can apply in real life. name: JB Pritzker
subject: I'll be blunt about NH.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Chris Pappas for Senate
body:
[](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/221?c0=em_ms_cp_20260330_2.l4TLXM&refcode=em20260330-2&t=1&akid=5854%2E582294%2EIp5qQT)
Governor JB Pritzker here.
Let me be blunt: **_Everything we care about is on the line in 2026 — and New Hampshire could decide the outcome._**
We’ve already seen the damage Trump’s second term is inflicting on our country: His ICE agents are once again targeting families in broad daylight -- tearing apart communities, rounding up workers, and instilling fear across entire neighborhoods. He’s gutting environmental protections while utility rates spike, forcing working families to foot the bill so his billionaire donors can cash out.
He has no interest in bipartisanship, decency, or democracy. **And if Democrats don’t take back the Senate this November, there will be nothing stopping him.** That’s why we _must_ win in New Hampshire.
**[Chris Pappas is running in a tied race that could decide Senate control. Chip in $5 now to help him win.](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260330_2.u0vejw&refcode=em20260330-2&t=2&akid=5854%2E582294%2EIp5qQT)**
Trump and his MAGA allies are laser-focused on New Hampshire. They’ve recruited a big-name candidate, they’re lining up GOP billionaire donors, and they know if they win here, they’ll shut the door on a Democratic Senate majority.
We can’t let that happen.
Chris Pappas is a fighter. He’s taken on Big Pharma, defended reproductive freedom, and delivered for working families in one of the toughest districts in the country.
I want him in the Senate. But we’re all going to have to come together to get him there. He’s running in a true battleground. His race is tied. And the GOP machine, desperate to keep Democrats locked out of power, is ready to bury him in dark money and attack ads.
**[That’s why I’m asking-- urgently -- for your help: Can you chip in $5 to help Chris Pappas win in New Hampshire and give us a fighting chance to stop Trump?](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260330_2.u0vejw&refcode=em20260330-2&t=3&akid=5854%2E582294%2EIp5qQT)**
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260330_2.u0vejw&amount=5&refcode=em20260330-2&t=22&akid=5854%2E582294%2EIp5qQT)**
The damage is real. The stakes are massive. And the time to act is right now.
Thank you for standing with Chris and for standing up to the madness.
JB Pritzker
Governor of Illinois
**New Hampshire is poised to be one of the closest Senate races in the country. Will you chip in today to help Chris stop the Republicans from flipping the Granite State red and expanding their Senate majority?**

body:
I never intended for things to end up like this. All I wanted to do was keep serving my country, the same way I have since I was sworn in to the U.S. Navy. |
# [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/128389959/611163034/336227065?refcode=em-header&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS85MDE1MyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkNjc5MTA1Mi02MjJjLWYxMTEtOWE0OC0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=T9LSbm6tM46kTySSxxjhD-edeYUA6Pbd8m54vLronLQ=)
Peter, when Gabby and I first agreed that I would run for Senate back in 2019, we knew things would change. We know more than most how public service can change your life.

But I’ve got to tell you, I never intended for things to end up like this. All I wanted to do was keep serving my country, the same way I have since I was sworn in to the U.S. Navy.

I know that service comes with risk, sure. But I didn’t set out to be threatened with a court-martial by the Secretary of Defense, or to have the President of the United States calling for my execution.

Look, I don’t want you to worry about me. I’ve been through a lot in my life, and things like this don’t intimidate me all that much.

I do worry that Trump might succeed at intimidating others, though. Like people just beginning to get involved, or thinking about joining a peaceful demonstration, or speaking out at a town hall. I worry Trump and his cronies are trying to scare people out of resisting him.

But then I see millions of people meeting this moment with the courage and resolve it demands of them. People like my friend George Whitesides. It makes me hopeful, sure. But more than that, it makes me incredibly proud.

We’re ready to fight like hell to save our democracy. If you’re with me, please:

**[Split a donation between me and George Whitesides. $10 or anything you can afford. The Atlantic: Donald Trump’s Plan to Subvert the Midterms Is Already Under Way [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=033026_2&amount=25]
Team, that headline from The Atlantic says it all.
Donald Trump already promised as part of his 2024 campaign that “we’ll have it fixed so good, you’re not gonna have to vote .” Watching his actions after he lost in 2020 -- lies, denial, rallies, all leading to January 6th -- it's not hard to imagine what he's got in mind for November.
Our states run our elections. But that doesn't mean that MAGA-aligned politicians won't follow his illegal orders to interfere. It doesn't stop him from using ICE agents to intimidate at the polls or threaten eligible voters. And it doesn't stop his Department of Justice from trying to interfere through the courts, especially when more than half of the suppressive lawsuits brought to court this year were brought by the very federal department that's supposed to protect our rights.
None of that takes into account the highly partisan efforts for mid-decade redistricting as well. It's clear that the threats to the next election aren't going to stop. That's where we come in.

name: Laura Lalemand
subject: Listening to the forests with science
body:
Dear Peter,

If redwood forests could speak, what would they say?

They might tell us their secrets about all the hidden life that burrows in the forest’s understory and perches on its redwood branches. We might learn how best to care for these long-lived giants and ensure the ecosystems that depend on them thrive.

Throughout Harold Richardson Redwoods Reserve, the forest is speaking. And thanks to you, we’re listening.

Save the Redwoods League is working to expand this extraordinary reserve with the help of our community. By acquiring 200 acres of adjacent land, we won’t just be preserving more old-growth redwoods—we’ll be strengthening a living laboratory for redwood science. [https://secure.savetheredwoods.org/a/donate-hrrrexpansion]

There are more than 373 species in the state that rely on these redwood forest ecosystems. To us, Harold Richardson Redwood Reserve is an escape... to northern spotted owls, steelhead trout, and marbled murrelets, the reserve is home.

To protect these native and endangered species, we’re conducting cutting-edge ecological research. [https://secure.savetheredwoods.org/a/donate-hrrrexpansion]
Make a Gift to Expand the Reserve [https://secure.savetheredwoods.org/a/donate-hrrrexpansion]

We listen to the forest with small, unobtrusive equipment called acoustic monitors. These microphones are secured to trees and are sensitive enough to pick up all the voices of the forest, even the wing flaps of birds.

These sounds tell us which species are nearby, where their main habitats are, and allow us to hear how they move throughout the forest. Learning about who’s present and their habitats allows us to minimize human disturbance in crucial wildlife areas.

Acoustic monitoring is one of several scientific studies we are taking part in at Harold Richardson Redwoods Reserve. Ongoing studies are looking at the role fog plays in the redwood ecosystem, how prescribed fires can restore and strengthen forest health—and more.

Will you make a special gift to help expand the Harold Richardson Redwoods Reserve and power essential ecological research? [https://secure.savetheredwoods.org/a/donate-hrrrexpansion]

The redwoods are speaking. With your help, we can continue to listen and act.

Sincerely,
Laura Lalemand
Senior Scientist

P.S. Please help us expand this incredible reserve and continue this important scientific work. [https://secure.savetheredwoods.org/a/donate-hrrrexpansion] With your help, we are taking steps forward and unraveling the secrets of the redwood forest—secrets that will help us preserve ecosystems up and down the redwood range.

Photos by Coldwater Collective

Acoustic monitoring is one of several scientific studies we are taking part in at Harold Richardson Redwoods Reserve. Ongoing studies are looking at the role fog plays in the redwood ecosystem, how prescribed fires can restore and strengthen forest health—and more. Will you make a special gift to help expand the Harold Richardson Redwoods Reserve and power essential ecological research? [] The redwoods are speaking. With your help, we can continue to listen and act. Sincerely, Laura Lalemand Senior Scientist P.S. Please help us expand this incredible reserve and continue this important scientific work. [] With your help, we are taking steps forward and unraveling the secrets of the redwood forest—secrets that will help us preserve ecosystems up and down the redwood range. Peter Willis,

THIS WEEK Bernie is expected to bring his bill to a vote to stop the Trump
administration from fast-tracking the sale of over 20,000 bombs – worth
$660 million – to Israel. And it’s up to ALL of us to stand with him.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/36266?source=email20260330&t=1011&akid=10466%2E5885482%2EtWlsGr ]Bernie Sanders on X describing the escalating conflicts in the Middle
East and why he introduced a bill to stop the U.S. from sending 20K+ more
bombs to Israel

Bernie is sounding the alarm over the horrific destruction Israel is
unleashing – made possible with U.S. weapons – not just in Gaza and Iran,
but in Lebanon and across the region. And now the Trump administration is
fast tracking even MORE weapons – without even bothering to get
Congressional approval. Enough.

We must not allow the US to continue enabling these horrors. Bernie filed
a Joint Resolution of Disapproval (JRD) to block the sale – and now the
vote is expected THIS WEEK.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/36266?source=email20260330&t=1012&akid=10466%2E5885482%2EtWlsGr ]Will you stand with Bernie and demand your members of Congress block
this sale and stop Trump from sending 20,000 MORE bombs to Israel that
will only bring more violence, more destruction, and more death?

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/36266?source=email20260330&t=1013&akid=10466%2E5885482%2EtWlsGr ]ADD YOUR NAME

Secretary of State Marco Rubio "waived" Congress’s right to review this
massive bomb sale, citing an "emergency." The deal includes 12,000 massive
1,000-pound bombs – the very types of bombs that have wiped out homes,
clinics, and schools in Gaza.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/36266?source=email20260330&t=1014&akid=10466%2E5885482%2EtWlsGr ]Headline: US argues 'Emergency' of Iran War means Israel needs 20,000+
more bombs without congressional approval

The truth is each time the U.S. sends weapons, the death toll goes up. We
have an obligation to say ENOUGH.

Trump has made it clear that Israel is in the driver's seat with this war,
saying ending the war will be a "mutual" decision with Netanyahu. But
Netanyahu’s government will only stop if we stop enabling them. So it’s up
to all of us to demand Congress block this bomb sale and demand
accountability.

Bernie has led these efforts before and gained more and more support each
time. This time, we can make it clear: America cannot be Israel’s supplier
of an endless cycle of violence, death, and displacement, funded by our
tax dollars.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/36266?source=email20260330&t=1015&akid=10466%2E5885482%2EtWlsGr ]Email Congress NOW: Stand with Bernie and demand they pass his JRD to
stop this arms deal before it’s too late.

(Erin Hooley/AP) (Yuri Gripas/Reuters)
By Illinois Review

Calls for federal scrutiny of Illinois’ finances intensified this week after Republican gubernatorial nominee Darren Bailey publicly urged the FBI and Department of Justice to investigate spending under Governor JB Pritzker.

Appearing on ‘My View with Lara Trump,’ Bailey pointed to what he described as widespread financial mismanagement in Illinois government.

“We’ve got waste and fraud at massive levels,” Bailey said. “I would love for the DoJ or the FBI to come in and investigate,” adding that the level of fraud is “immense.”

His comments come as broader concerns grow over state spending and accountability in Illinois, particularly in light of recent federal investigations in Minnesota that uncovered billions of dollars in alleged fraud tied to government programs.

In Minnesota, federal authorities have warned that the schemes uncovered may only be the “tip of the iceberg,” prompting renewed scrutiny in other states with large budgets and long-standing one-party control.

Illinois is increasingly part of that conversation.

Since taking office, Gov. Pritzker has overseen a significant expansion in state spending. Illinois’ General Funds budget has grown by nearly $20 billion – rising from approximately $36 billion in Fiscal Year 2019 to about $55 billion today.

Despite that increase, critics argue that residents have not seen meaningful improvements in core services.

Property taxes remain among the highest in the nation. Public safety concerns continue in major urban areas. Education outcomes in some districts still lag behind national benchmarks. At the same time, Illinois has experienced ongoing population loss and business departures.
https://www.illinoisreview.com/illinoisreview/2026/03/bailey-calls-for-fbi-probe-into-pritzker-spending-during-lara-trump-interview-citing-immense-fraud.html?utm_source=Illinois+Review&utm_campaign=7d6e9b0d69-EMAIL_CAMPAIGN_2023_10_30_09_24_COPY_01&utm_medium=email&utm_term=0_-8b40ac336f-666344823
A behind-the-scenes look at Lara Trump interviewing Darren Bailey at Trump Tower Chicago. (Photo: Illinois Review)
Beyond overall spending levels, questions have also been raised about how taxpayer dollars are being allocated.

Public reporting has highlighted that more than $20 billion in state contracts have been awarded to a relatively small group of firms with ties to Pritzker’s broader financial network since 2019.

Additionally, more than $180 million in taxpayer-backed investments have been directed toward projects linked to the governor’s family hotel interests through state entities.

There have been no formal findings of wrongdoing tied to those expenditures. However, the scale and concentration of the spending have drawn increased attention from watchdog groups and political observers.

Bailey’s call for federal involvement reflects a growing push among some Republicans and government accountability advocates for outside oversight.

Those concerns have also reached the national stage.

X () Facebook () IllinoisReview.com () Bailey Calls for FBI Probe Into Pritzker Spending During Lara Trump Interview, Citing “Immense” Fraud () (Erin Hooley/AP) (Yuri Gripas/Reuters) By Illinois Review Calls for federal scrutiny of Illinois’ finances intensified this week after Republican gubernatorial nominee Darren Bailey publicly urged the FBI and Department of Justice to investigate spending under Governor JB Pritzker. Appearing on ‘My View with Lara Trump,’ Bailey pointed to what he described as widespread financial mismanagement in Illinois government. “We’ve got waste and fraud at massive levels,” Bailey said. “I would love for the DoJ or the FBI to come in and investigate,” adding that the level of fraud is “immense.” His comments come as broader concerns grow over state spending and accountability in Illinois, particularly in light of recent federal investigations in Minnesota that uncovered billions of dollars in alleged fraud tied to government programs. In Minnesota, federal authorities have warned that the schemes uncovered may only be the “tip of the iceberg,” prompting renewed scrutiny in other states with large budgets and long-standing one-party control. Illinois is increasingly part of that conversation. Since taking office, Gov. Pritzker has overseen a significant expansion in state spending. Illinois’ General Funds budget has grown by nearly $20 billion – rising from approximately $36 billion in Fiscal Year 2019 to about $55 billion today. Despite that increase, critics argue that residents have not seen meaningful improvements in core services. Property taxes remain among the highest in the nation. Public safety concerns continue in major urban areas. Education outcomes in some districts still lag behind national benchmarks. At the same time, Illinois has experienced ongoing population loss and business departures. A behind-the-scenes look at Lara Trump interviewing Darren Bailey at Trump Tower Chicago. (Photo: Illinois Review) Beyond overall spending levels, questions have also been raised about how taxpayer dollars are being allocated. Public reporting has highlighted that more than $20 billion in state contracts have been awarded to a relatively small group of firms with ties to Pritzker’s broader financial network since 2019. Additionally, more than $180 million in taxpayer-backed investments have been directed toward projects linked to the governor’s family hotel interests through state entities. There have been no formal findings of wrongdoing tied to those expenditures. However, the scale and concentration of the spending have drawn increased attention from watchdog groups and political observers. Bailey’s call for federal involvement reflects a growing push among some Republicans and government accountability advocates for outside oversight. Those concerns have also reached the national stage. I wanted to make sure you saw the latest poll in our race, because it’s a big deal:

This campaign is about bringing Californians together to fight for an affordable and just future—but we have to reach more voters _now_ if we’re going to win. **[Can you chip in $5 to help us spread our message before it’s too late?](https://act.katieporter.com/go/21531?c0=em_ms_kp_20260330_1_ak.0NoIEr&refcode=em20260330-41060&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=4&akid=41060%2E3422442%2Efxpu7H)**

Here’s what this poll shows: the two candidates ahead of me are MAGA extremists that will follow Trump’s orders. The candidates behind me are Democrats who are bankrolled by big money. _One of them is even a billionaire funding his own campaign._
**I’m the only candidate running to put working Californians first.**
I’m a single mom who knows what it’s like to stretch a budget and drive an old car. As governor, I’ll work to lower costs and make life better for families like ours, not do the bidding of corporations or Donald Trump.
This race will be close, and I need your help to hold the corporate and MAGA candidates accountable. We only have a few weeks to win over undecided voters, and I’m counting on people like you to step up and help us reach them.

Katie Porter

subject: This wasn’t the plan
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Democratic Association of Secretaries of State, Treasurer Denise Merrill
body:
I never intended for things to end up like this. All I wanted to do was keep serving my country, the same way I have since I was sworn in to the U.S. Navy. | Team, when Gabby and I first agreed that I would run for Senate back in 2019, we knew things would change. We know more than most how public service can change your life. But I’ve got to tell you, I never intended for things to end up like this. All I wanted to do was keep serving my country, the same way I have since I was sworn in to the U.S. Navy. I know that service comes with risk, sure. But I didn’t set out to be threatened with a court-martial by the Secretary of Defense, or to have the President of the United States calling for my execution. Look, I don’t want you to worry about me. I’ve been through a lot in my life, and things like this don’t intimidate me all that much. I do worry that Trump might succeed at intimidating others, though. Like people just beginning to get involved, or thinking about joining a peaceful demonstration, or speaking out at a town hall. I worry Trump and his cronies are trying to scare people out of resisting him. But then I see millions of people meeting this moment with the courage and resolve it demands of them. People like the Democratic Association of Secretaries of State. It makes me hopeful, sure. But more than that, it makes me incredibly proud. We’re ready to fight like hell to save our democracy. # [](https://act.chrisforjustice.com/go/18?refcode=em20260330-1310&t=1&akid=1313%2E294397%2ENmRUCt)
We wish this election were as simple as the most qualified candidate winning.
If it were, Judge Chris Taylor — someone with decades of experience fighting for fairness and justice — would already have this race locked up.
But that’s not how it works.
**The truth is, right-wing special interests can jump in at any moment, spend millions, and reach tons of undecided voters before we do.**
We’ve seen it happen before, and with this seat deciding the future of our Wisconsin Supreme Court, there’s no telling what could happen in these final few days.
**That’s why we’re counting on grassroots support to stay on the offense and be prepared for the worst-case scenario.**

We can put an end to the GOP majority by electing leaders who put working people first. | | | Peter, If we’re going to defeat Trumpism, we need to take back as much power from Republicans in Congress as we can. _**Contributions Made by an Individual or Federal Non-Multicandidate Political Committee:**_
Individuals or federal non-multicandidate PACs may contribute up to $322,100. Such contributions shall be allocated in the following order:
1\. Campaign shall receive any contribution not exceeding $7,000, designating up to $3,500 to the primary election and up to $3,500 to the general election, provided such limits apply.

_**Contributions Made by a Federal Multicandidate Political Committee:**_
Multicandidate PACs may contribute up to $120,000. Such contributions shall be allocated in the following order:
1\. Campaign shall receive any contribution not exceeding $10,000, designating up to $5,000 to the primary election and up to $5,000 to the general election, provided such limits apply.

5 .NRCC shall receive any contribution not to exceed $45,000 for its Legal Proceedings Fund, provided such limits apply.

Contributions that exceed a donor's contribution limit to a participating Committee shall be reallocated to the remaining Committees according to this allocation formula to the extent permitted by FECA. Any contributor may designate his or her contribution to a specific participant Committee to the extent permitted by FECA. Federal law requires us to use our best efforts to collect and report the name, mailing address, occupation, and name of employer of each individual whose aggregate contributions exceed $200 in an election cycle or calendar year, as applicable.

clean_body: Anyone who’s read the news this month can probably infer that Republicans are in serious trouble Anyone who’s read the news this month can probably infer that Republicans are in serious trouble | | | | | Peter, 🚨 OUR FUNDRAISING HAS HIT A SNAG 🚨 Can you spare $32, Peter? That 's our average donation in March so far -- and it's exactly what it will take to help us stay competitive and keep Texas red. Our fundraising has fallen off, and honestly, it's happening at a TERRIBLE time. We're preparing to report our 1st quarter fundraising numbers to the FEC, and we can't leave a single penny on the table. By now, you've probably heard: Republicans are in serious trouble here in Texas. Earlier this month, Democrats turned out in massive numbers, more than Republicans for the first time in recent memory, with over 2.3 million casting ballots in their Senate primary. Radical James Talarico emerged as their nominee, fresh off raising millions in record time, and national Democrats are already pouring in cash to make him competitive and flip the Lone Star State blue. They want to erase everything we've built here and end our 32-year winning streak for the first time since 1994. We cannot let that happen. So far this month, 430 conservatives have chipped in, averaging $32 each. It's not going to be enough to help us finish out the first quarter. That's why I'm imploring you to help me today. If we don't remain competitive, it could be the end of the line for Republicans in Texas. Can you make a $32 contribution right now? It would mean so much to us. Peter, I don't want to fight alone. If it's been a while since you've donated, I understand. But if you still believe in what we've fought for -- secure borders, tax relief, strong judges, and keeping Texas red -- I'm asking you to show up today. Your $32 will enable me to keep fighting for Texas values while pushing back against the radical left. Your name on our donor list shows we're not fighting alone. Thousands of grassroots donors pledging our average March donation sends a powerful message:__Conservative Republicans are energized and unshaken -- and we will not let our streak end. I'm in this fight to keep Texas red and bring common sense back to Washington. Please stand with me in this critical moment. Good Evening,

If we haven't met, my name is Sam Williams. I'm the political director for Mayor Chaz Molder's campaign for the 5th congressional district.

You are receiving this email as you have expressed interest in volunteering with our campaign in some capacity. We are incredibly grateful for your interest and support.

While it is still early and we are not knocking doors/making phone calls yet, there is still lots to be done right now!

Please join us on _**Thursday, April 2nd at 3pm**_ for a virtual campaign update with Mayor Molder, our campaign manager Jasmine Singh and I.

We look forward to connecting with y'all. Invite to follow.

Thanks and please let me know if you have any questions.

Best,
Sam

body:
| Peter, it’s Abigail Spanberger.

I never expected to run for office, but in 2018, I stepped up and ran for Congress in a district that hadn’t elected a Democrat since 1968 — and we won.

That year marked a real turning point. A wave of new leaders — including a record number of women — stepped up, flipped long-held Republican districts, and made it clear that the old way of doing things in Washington wasn’t going to cut it anymore.

My good friend Angie Craig and I were both elected as part of that historic Congressional class — a group united by a shared commitment to do things differently and deliver real results for the people we serve.

Over my three terms in Congress, I saw firsthand how Angie shows up and fights every single day — for her district, for working families, and for what’s right. It’s exactly why I know she’s the kind of leader Minnesota needs in the U.S. Senate.
---

That fight isn’t new for Angie. She grew up in a mobile home park, raised by a single mom, and worked two jobs to put herself through college.

She’s never backed down from tough fights — from winning a landmark case to adopt her son and protect the rights of LGBTQ+ families, to standing up in Congress against Donald Trump’s chaos and corruption by voting to impeach him twice.

And she’s delivered real results, including taking on Big Pharma and writing the bill that capped insulin at $35 a month.

Last November, I flipped the Virginia Governor's seat and showed what’s possible — when Democrats come together around real leadership and a clear purpose, we win.

[**Now, Minnesota has the opportunity to build on that same kind of momentum by electing Angie Craig to the U.S. Senate — and Democrats have no shot of taking back the Senate without holding this seat. So, I’m asking you to take the next step with us. I had the pleasure of going to Nashville again last weekend.
Absolutely love coming home. To me it will always be home. There is just a special feeling and vibe Nashville has. There is magic in the air and it's bursting with creativity.

I had the opportunity to be creative again when I was invited to do a singer songwriter night at the Commodore on West End. It's a place where lots of locals go and some very talented writers and musicians. I had the honor to be on stage with some of my dearest friends.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9oZWFydGxhbmRqb3VybmFsLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.kaq0qCWEbtkIiiRbqyaf48IQvyU3_dyOca3vYFMd_Os?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=192646584)
Sandra Lee who is so talented and very well connected and is an absolute blast to be around. We have been friends for 20 years! When we get together it's always an adventure. She sang one of her songs called "Girls will be girls". It's about 2 women who are always up to something. 2 hot messes. Wonder who she was talking about :)

Another was Joe Webber. He was my Bass player and band leader. We had worked together 25 years; touring the country and parts of the world. Oh do we have some stories to tell. Some crazy things we have experienced. Whenever we get together you will find us telling stories and bursting out laughing.

Being up on stage again and singing to an audience after so long was a Rush! But what was even better was just being present. Watching all the people and singing my heart out with some of my besties on the stage and some in the audience; including my precious daughter. She enjoyed just hanging out watching all the activities and taking videos.

We then drove downtown Nashville and she was amazed with all the lights and people everywhere. I guess i took for granted that she had been there. I know I had taken her downtown but I guess she was too young to remember. Just seeing her eyes light up was an ending of a great night.

Even though Nashville is such a big city that looks like Vegas it still has its charm, and that is all the beautiful people that make it unique and one of a kind...

Caramel Pecan Bars

**INGREDIENTS**
* 1 1/2 cups old fashioned oats
* 1 1/2 cups flour
* 1 1/4 cups brown sugar
* 3/4 tsp baking soda
* 1/4 tsp salt
* 3/4 cups butter softened
* 1 package (14oz0 caramels
* 1/2 cup whipping cream
* 1 1/2 cups semisweet chocolate chips
* 3/4 cups chopped pecans

**DIRECTIONS**
In a bowl, combine the first five ingredients; stir in butter and mix till crumbly.
Set aside 1 cup for topping.
Press remaining mixture into a greased 13 in x9 in pan.
Bake at 350* for 10 mins. Meanwhile, combine caramels and cream in a heavy saucepan. Cook over low heat until caramels are melted. Stir often.
Sprinkle chocolate chips and nuts over hot crust; top with caramel mixture. Sprinkle with reserved oat mixture. Bake for 350* for 20 minutes or until topping is golden brown. Cool completely before cutting. Enjoy!

# [](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/43706?t=1&akid=240774%2E444211%2E-BYYY-)
I feel almost silly writing this, because when I get an “end-of-quarter deadline” request for a donation (they’re filling my inbox as you read this), my eyes start to roll.
What’s different about the end-of-quarter versus any other day of the month?
I can’t speak to all the candidates and campaigns that are bombarding your inbox right now.
But I can tell you that in Powered by People we have a budget that dictates what I can spend on organizers, supporting volunteers, traveling — in other words, doing the work behind reaching, registering and turning out the voters we need to win political power in Texas.
If we don’t meet that budget, I can’t hire more organizers (we have 13 right now covering the entire state — that means one organizer is covering the entire Panhandle, North Texas and West Texas just short of El Paso county. Imagine what we could do with 20 organizers!). It’s all a function of money. The more I raise, the more I can do.
Remember, we turned donations like yours in 2024 into one of the most successful turnout pilots in the country.
Young Texans that we met on campuses across the state — listening to them, registering them and staying in touch with them throughout the election — turned out at a rate of over 79%! To put that in context, young voter turnout in Texas outside of our program was 37%.
[**This is the work that works. And I’d be grateful for your support right now as we try to close the books on March ahead of budget.**](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/56109?c0=pbp-em-20260330-1.2XBEtl&refcode=ema20260330-240774&t=3&akid=240774%2E444211%2E-BYYY-)

Aloha Peter, Recently, communities across Hawaii were hit hard by severe flooding. Families have lost homes, communities went without power, and neighborhoods needed to be evacuated. Though these storm systems pummeled the state, Hawaii communities also came together to help their neighbors and their neighborhoods; clearing debris, removing mud, and helping people deal with the fallout of water that reached chest high in some places. Yet, more can be done. If you’d like to assist in this effort and help Hawaii begin to rebuild from the awful devastation caused by recent flooding, I’ve included some resources below where you can offer help to those who desperately need it. clean_body: | Aloha Peter, Recently, communities across Hawaii were hit hard by severe flooding. Families have lost homes, communities went without power, and neighborhoods needed to be evacuated. Though these storm systems pummeled the state, Hawaii communities also came together to help their neighbors and their neighborhoods; clearing debris, removing mud, and helping people deal with the fallout of water that reached chest high in some places. Yet, more can be done. If you’d like to assist in this effort and help Hawaii begin to rebuild from the awful devastation caused by recent flooding, I’ve included some resources below where you can offer help to those who desperately need it. Please stay safe, lean on each other, and know that we’ll get through this. Mahalo, Mazie Aloha United Way: The Aloha United Way’s provides emergency assistance for basic needs like food, shelter, and healthcare, helping individuals and families regain stability during times of crisis. American Red Cross: The American Red Cross is providing disaster relief to those affected by the storms and floods in Hawaii. Hawaii Community Foundation: The Hawaii Community Foundation’s is a dedicated fund designed to support statewide disaster and emergency-related preparedness, response, recovery, mitigation, and resilience. Hawaii Island United Way: The is accepting donations to assist communities impacted by the floods, asking supporters to make a note in their donation that they want to support flood relief. Hawaiian Humane Society: The is accepting resources to support the pets and people of Oʻahu throughout this recovery. Friends of Mazie Hirono 335 Merchant Street #677 Honolulu, HI 96809 United States mailto:info@mazieforhawaii.com | Paid for by Mazie Hirono For Hawaii

Hartzell Gray is a strong, progressive champion for the people of Missouri. And when Republicans, under orders from President Trump, gerrymandered our congressional districts, Hartzell didn't back down.
Now he's running in MO-04 against Mark Alford to prove that our movement can succeed even when the Republicans are so afraid of it, they try every underhanded trick in the book to stop it.

It’s about a system in which politicians choose their voters, rather than voters choosing their leaders. It’s about creeping Trump-style authoritarianism taking hold at the state level.

Cori Bush and Hartzell Gray are two of the only progressive candidates in Missouri standing up for voters by running on platforms that actually meet this moment. Together, we’re working towards:

* Ending the genocide in Gaza
* Abolishing ICE
* Taxing the rich to pay for public programs
* Reparations to confront the legacy of slavery
* Protecting our reproductive care from attacks by Republicans
* Guaranteeing housing as a human right
* Delivering higher wages and union jobs

_### Begin Forwarded Message ###_

Hi Peter,

Most families don’t get 100 days to figure out how they’re going to pay their bills. They get 30.

That’s why today, I’m introducing my 30-Day Plan: a transparent, concrete agenda for what I will accomplish in my first month as Governor of Wisconsin.

No vague promises. No platitudes. Just results.

Here’s what’s on my agenda:
* **Repeal Act 10** in order to restore collective bargaining rights for all Wisconsin workers
* **Close the special education funding gap** so school districts aren't forced to cut programs and lay off teachers to make up the difference
* **Pass universal Pre-K and childcare** utilizing the existing providers already serving Wisconsin families
* **Open BadgerCare as a public health option** for every Wisconsin family
* **Strengthen and fund domestic violence prevention and crisis support** across rural and urban Wisconsin

## Flight Attendant’s Miracle Survival
A flight attendant was [ejected from an Air Canada jet](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGSsyAUBeCn0Q4HQUULir-xy99uydzARW8GJQNEN3n6nWQfYeszc8585-tiLkCB9uU_bKj94k3x0ex45oClYDIbJbABbYK85kc66IjJQghgBBcD45JJbhxQeJq-dtojCpQ16lapbuLtpPp61X5QIHpvrequFkWLXky9c-N16gdrR6xJv9u4lFzwdpJdM4wTV0r60batAjVVHUdHJabmFmkvK_rwjAemxsatDnot5Z4r-a8ScyXm8zwbH7_findeifmRKzEHWB6QHAH7aBhQYhZ2cMBu8HoxH2hZC4NScHewF_brxVwn7e4nhUB5UFXHlw0ofJbLny87tPgJAAD__11KhL0) that crashed into a fire truck at LaGuardia Airport Sunday night and survived. Solange Tremblay was found more than 300 feet from the wreckage, still strapped into her jump seat. Her daughter called it a "[complete miracle](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkMGOnSAYhZ8Gd9z8gIouWNxM6s6mSRddGgZ-lCnCBBiNffrG20fo8iQnJ-f7fs3LrH3wcf2ud1RudUt1aYl4loC1Yl52n7UJaLIuW_nKhz9SNjoEvXDgPQVBBSxW-3AtXWOVQ-QoGlRMynYENsqu2RRYZkCwnpt3GKThzImeGcHNOx8613eNV_caCAEc2CjaRz-MIKVwg2FMajmSFtD6mvLjI_lYN3ThSgfmh0l7E9RW62ch4kn4RPh0nuejfMV4ld_Xn7tB-LSmZOnNRfjUMz4SPlEQI33S-R_hK73pqK3XkU7Br1ulz1oxWh0r_faBpqKlDIDOWDEXOuW00x9BR6Q_X2aw0LfbU5OV_Tx9CL70krSw7tqH19P634oPxf8GAAD__6wSkM8)." Experts say the crew seat's four-point restraint system, designed to withstand far greater crash forces than a passenger seat, likely saved her life. Tremblay suffered leg fractures and will need surgery but is expected to recover. _**by Dr. Eric Lullove, Blue Amp Media, Contributing Medical Editor**_
In my 20-plus years as a surgical podiatrist and wound care specialist, I've learned one immutable truth: you cannot heal a systemic infection by ignoring the primary site of the wound. Yet, that is exactly what this administration is attempting to do.
The recent announcement that the Department of Defense (DOD) is requesting a supplemental $200 billion for the war effort is a clinical failure of priorities. While the Pentagon asks for a massive infusion of capital to "replenish stockpiles" and fuel conflict in Iran, our domestic healthcare infrastructure is being subjected to a radical, unguided amputation.
## The Anatomy of a Budgetary Crisis
As a physician, I look at data. When we look at the Fiscal Year 2026 budget, the "pathology report" for American healthcare is grim. The administration isn't just trimming "waste"--they are cutting into healthy tissue.
1. The NIH Is Flatlining: The proposed $18 billion cut to the NIH is a direct assault on the future of medicine. We are talking about halting research into regenerative medicine and chronic disease--the very advancements that keep you and me walking and out of the OR.
2. The CDC Is Being Gutted: A $3.6 billion reduction means we are surrendering our surveillance systems. In an era of global health threats, we are choosing to spend on missiles while leaving our front doors unlocked against the next pandemic.
3. CMS and the ACA: The "machete" approach to CMS and the ACA is already resulting in coverage gaps. For my patients in Florida, these "structural cuts" aren't just numbers on a spreadsheet; they are the reason a foot ulcer or hypertension or diabetes goes untreated until it's too late.
* * *

* * *

## $200 Billion: The Opportunity Cost of "Lethality"
Let's put that $200 billion in perspective. In the wound care world, we fight for every cent of reimbursement to ensure patients get advanced biologics and life-saving therapies.
The $200 billion DOD request represents a 1,100% surplus over what is needed to simply keep our domestic health agencies at their current levels. By choosing to "armor up" abroad while "cutting out" the heart of our medical research and preventive care at home, we are effectively buying a gold-plated suit of armor for a body that is suffering from untreated sepsis.
The $200 billion requested for the DOD is:
More than double the entire annual budget for HHS.
Enough to fully fund the NIH for the next four years.
Sufficient to clear the entire backlog of veteran healthcare claims ten times over.
Secretary Hegseth says we need to be "tippy-top" in military lethality. But as a doctor, I have to ask: What is the point of being the most "lethal" nation on earth if our own citizens are dying from preventable chronic diseases because we've defunded the agencies meant to protect them?

## How This Affects the VA
The impact of a $200 billion Department of Defense supplemental request on the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) is a classic case of what we call "secondary intention" in surgery--when a wound is left to heal on its own because the resources are being diverted elsewhere.
While the VA budget for 2026 is actually slated for a 10% increase (reaching roughly $441 billion), that $200 billion DOD request is a "phantom limb" that highlights exactly where our national priorities are skewed. As a physician who treats veterans, I see the gap between "fully funded" on paper and the reality of clinical care.
The VA "Wound": Infrastructure and Backlogs
If we redirected even a fraction of that $200 billion "war chest" to the VA, we could address the chronic systemic issues that a 10% annual increase barely touches:
* The Infrastructure Crisis: The VA currently has a $170 billion backlog in capital needs. Most VA hospitals were built decades ago and are struggling with outdated HVAC, plumbing, and electrical systems. For the price of this one DOD request, we could literally rebuild every crumbling VA medical center in the country.
* The Claims Backlog: Despite the PACT Act, the Veterans Benefits Administration (VBA) is still fighting a massive surge in claims. Veterans' organizations (DAV and VFW) have noted that the VA lacks the internal capacity to meet rising demand. A $200 billion investment could modernize the entire AI-enabled claims system and eliminate wait times for life-altering benefits.
* Medical Research: The VA's Medical and Prosthetic Research budget is only about $943 million. We are spending 200 times that amount on a single war supplemental. As a podiatrist, I know that research into limb salvage and prosthetic innovation is what keeps our wounded warriors mobile--but it's being treated as a rounding error compared to munitions.

* * *

## Why This Matters for Every American
When the NIH loses nearly 40% of its budget, we lose the next decade of breakthroughs in cancer, Alzheimer's, and diabetes. When the CDC is forced to stop focusing on chronic diseases--the leading killers in this country--the burden of late-stage complications falls squarely on our local hospitals and your family's wallet.
We are being told we must choose "Lethality" over "Longevity." I reject that premise. A nation that cannot fund its own health is not a nation that is truly secure, no matter how many missiles are in the silo.
In the OR, if I see a surgeon making a cut that will lead to a permanent disability, it is my job to speak up. This $200 billion request is that wrong cut. It's time we demand a budget that prioritizes the longevity of our citizens over the lethality of our weapons.
_Dr. Lullove is the Chief Executive and Medical Officer of the West Boca Center for Wound Healing in Coconut Creek, FL. He is a national health care policy expert and expert in wound healing. He is the Contributing Medical Editor for Blue Amp Media._

The administration funds missiles while medicine is gutted | | and | Mar 30 | | | ---|---|--- | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- Cliff 's Note: Blue Amp Media is independent progressive journalism powered by readers like you. If this piece moves you, become part of our community -- . by Dr. Eric Lullove, Blue Amp Media, Contributing Medical Editor In my 20-plus years as a surgical podiatrist and wound care specialist, I've learned one immutable truth: you cannot heal a systemic infection by ignoring the primary site of the wound. Yet, that is exactly what this administration is attempting to do. The recent announcement that the Department of Defense (DOD) is requesting a supplemental $200 billion for the war effort is a clinical failure of priorities. While the Pentagon asks for a massive infusion of capital to "replenish stockpiles" and fuel conflict in Iran, our domestic healthcare infrastructure is being subjected to a radical, unguided amputation. The Anatomy of a Budgetary Crisis As a physician, I look at data. When we look at the Fiscal Year 2026 budget, the "pathology report" for American healthcare is grim. The administration isn't just trimming "waste"--they are cutting into healthy tissue. 1. The NIH Is Flatlining: The proposed $18 billion cut to the NIH is a direct assault on the future of medicine. We are talking about halting research into regenerative medicine and chronic disease--the very advancements that keep you and me walking and out of the OR. 2. The CDC Is Being Gutted: A $3.6 billion reduction means we are surrendering our surveillance systems. In an era of global health threats, we are choosing to spend on missiles while leaving our front doors unlocked against the next pandemic. 3. CMS and the ACA: The "machete" approach to CMS and the ACA is already resulting in coverage gaps. For my patients in Florida, these "structural cuts" aren't just numbers on a spreadsheet; they are the reason a foot ulcer or hypertension or diabetes goes untreated until it's too late. $200 Billion: The Opportunity Cost of "Lethality" Let's put that $200 billion in perspective. In the wound care world, we fight for every cent of reimbursement to ensure patients get advanced biologics and life-saving therapies. The $200 billion DOD request represents a 1,100% surplus over what is needed to simply keep our domestic health agencies at their current levels. By choosing to "armor up" abroad while "cutting out" the heart of our medical research and preventive care at home, we are effectively buying a gold-plated suit of armor for a body that is suffering from untreated sepsis. The $200 billion requested for the DOD is: More than double the entire annual budget for HHS. Enough to fully fund the NIH for the next four years. Sufficient to clear the entire backlog of veteran healthcare claims ten times over. Secretary Hegseth says we need to be "tippy-top" in military lethality. But as a doctor, I have to ask: What is the point of being the most "lethal" nation on earth if our own citizens are dying from preventable chronic diseases because we've defunded the agencies meant to protect them? How This Affects the VA The impact of a $200 billion Department of Defense supplemental request on the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) is a classic case of what we call "secondary intention" in surgery--when a wound is left to heal on its own because the resources are being diverted elsewhere. While the VA budget for 2026 is actually slated for a 10% increase (reaching roughly $441 billion), that $200 billion DOD request is a "phantom limb" that highlights exactly where our national priorities are skewed. As a physician who treats veterans, I see the gap between "fully funded" on paper and the reality of clinical care. The VA "Wound": Infrastructure and Backlogs If we redirected even a fraction of that $200 billion "war chest" to the VA, we could address the chronic systemic issues that a 10% annual increase barely touches: The Infrastructure Crisis: The VA currently has a $170 billion backlog in capital needs. Most VA hospitals were built decades ago and are struggling with outdated HVAC, plumbing, and electrical systems. For the price of this one DOD request, we could literally rebuild every crumbling VA medical center in the country. The Claims Backlog: Despite the PACT Act, the Veterans Benefits Administration (VBA) is still fighting a massive surge in claims. Veterans' organizations (DAV and VFW) have noted that the VA lacks the internal capacity to meet rising demand. A $200 billion investment could modernize the entire AI-enabled claims system and eliminate wait times for life-altering benefits. Medical Research: The VA's Medical and Prosthetic Research budget is only about $943 million. We are spending 200 times that amount on a single war supplemental. As a podiatrist, I know that research into limb salvage and prosthetic innovation is what keeps our wounded warriors mobile--but it's being treated as a rounding error compared to munitions. Why This Matters for Every American When the NIH loses nearly 40% of its budget, we lose the next decade of breakthroughs in cancer, Alzheimer's, and diabetes. When the CDC is forced to stop focusing on chronic diseases--the leading killers in this country--the burden of late-stage complications falls squarely on our local hospitals and your family's wallet. We are being told we must choose "Lethality" over "Longevity." I reject that premise. A nation that cannot fund its own health is not a nation that is truly secure, no matter how many missiles are in the silo. In the OR, if I see a surgeon making a cut that will lead to a permanent disability, it is my job to speak up. This $200 billion request is that wrong cut. It's time we demand a budget that prioritizes the longevity of our citizens over the lethality of our weapons. Dr. Lullove is the Chief Executive and Medical Officer of the West Boca Center for Wound Healing in Coconut Creek, FL. He is a national health care policy expert and expert in wound healing. Hey team, There are two Americas right now. One where the well-connected and wealthy get tax breaks, bend the rules, and avoid consequences. And another where people are turning down their heat because they can’t afford the utility bills, where families are struggling to figure out how to get by. But it goes beyond just finance and economics. There’s an America that feels bound by the law, but not protected by it. That’s what we’re hearing from voters and seeing on the ground: people who feel like the rules apply to them, but not to the people at the top. And then there’s an America that feels protected by the law, but not bound by it — where people at the very top operate like the rules don’t apply to them. We’ve seen this before. In 2008, executives crashed the economy, millions of Americans lost their homes and savings, and almost no one at the top was held accountable. The system stepped in to bail them out, and then moved on. It’s the same story when it comes to Epstein: a network of powerful people who never took responsibility, years of abuse, and victims who never got real closure. That can’t be how this country works. This campaign is about standing up for the people living in that second America, economically and when it comes to the rule of law, and making clear that no one is above it. And if it’s done right, it’s not just about drawing that contrast. clean_body: And that's a problem. | | Hey team, There are two Americas right now. One where the well-connected and wealthy get tax breaks, bend the rules, and avoid consequences. And another where people are turning down their heat because they can’t afford the utility bills, where families are struggling to figure out how to get by. But it goes beyond just finance and economics. There’s an America that feels bound by the law, but not protected by it. That’s what we’re hearing from voters and seeing on the ground: people who feel like the rules apply to them, but not to the people at the top. And then there’s an America that feels protected by the law, but not bound by it — where people at the very top operate like the rules don’t apply to them. We’ve seen this before. In 2008, executives crashed the economy, millions of Americans lost their homes and savings, and almost no one at the top was held accountable. The system stepped in to bail them out, and then moved on. It’s the same story when it comes to Epstein: a network of powerful people who never took responsibility, years of abuse, and victims who never got real closure. That can’t be how this country works. This campaign is about standing up for the people living in that second America, economically and when it comes to the rule of law, and making clear that no one is above it. And if it’s done right, it’s not just about drawing that contrast. It’s about bringing those two Americas back under the same standard. = | = | = ---|--- = | = = | = If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your secure donation will go through immediately.
